2026-12-06.title: Sunday of the Birth of John the Baptist
readings: Hannah gives Samuel to the Lord
Children are a heritage from the Lord
You shall be called by a new name
2026-12-06.alt: Fourth Sunday of Suboro. The Twenty-Five Days Nombu continues.
2026-12-06.verse: And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways.
theo: Elizabeth's time comes and she bears a son. The neighbours rejoice, because “the Lord had shown his great mercy to her”. The child whose birth seemed impossible is born, and his name is chosen not by custom but by God: “His name is John”, which means “God is gracious”.

For nine months Zechariah had been silent. When he writes “His name is John” on a tablet, obeying the angel's word, “immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue freed, and he began to speak, praising God.” Doubt had closed his mouth; obedience opens it. His first words are praise, the Benedictus that the Church still prays every morning: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favorably on his people and redeemed them.”

The Old Testament readings show God's way with children of promise. Moses was drawn out of the water to deliver his people. Hannah, who prayed for a son, gives him back: “For this child I prayed… therefore I have lent him to the LORD” (1 Samuel 1:27–28). The psalm says: “Sons are indeed a heritage from the LORD, the fruit of the womb a reward.” Every child is a gift and has a mission from God.

Zechariah's song ends looking towards Christ: “By the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death.” John is not the light; he prepares for the Dawn. The Church in this season is called to the same task: to point beyond herself to Christ who comes.
conn: Three children, one pattern.
Moses, Samuel and John: each born in a dark time, each given to God from the beginning, each preparing God's people for a new beginning.
A name from God.
God changes or chooses names to show a mission: Abram becomes Abraham (Genesis 17:5), and Isaiah promises Jerusalem “a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give” (Isaiah 62:2).
The Benedictus and the Magnificat.
Mary sang after the Visitation, Zechariah after John's birth. Both songs bless God for remembering his covenant with Abraham.
Children of the promise.
Paul contrasts the children of slavery and of promise (Galatians 4:28). John, born by God's promise, prepares for the One who makes us all children of the promise.
altar: Zechariah's tongue was loosed to bless God. At every Holy Qurbono our tongues too are freed for praise, and we receive the One whom John announced: “the dawn from on high” comes to us under the signs of bread and wine.
outline: Ask: what is the meaning of your name, and who chose it?
God is gracious. A child's name is a vocation, not only a family tradition.
Zechariah's tongue is freed when he obeys. Our doubts close us; obedience opens us to praise.
Point 3 · Every child is a gift
Moses, Samuel, John; Psalm 127. A word for parents and for the unborn.
The Benedictus: we, like John, point beyond ourselves to Christ.
“God is gracious; I will prepare his way.”
live: Bless God each morning (Luke 1:68)
Pray the Benedictus, or at least its first verse, every morning this week.
Pray for children (Psalm 127:3)
Bless each child in your home by name with the sign of the cross before they sleep.
Prepare the way
Make a good Confession during this Nombu, so that Christ finds a straight path to your heart.
fathers: St Augustine
John was the voice, Christ the Word. The voice passes, the Word remains; John speaks so that the Word may be heard (Sermon 293).
St Bede the Venerable
He explains that Zechariah's tongue was loosed when he confirmed the name given by God, and that the Church sings his canticle daily to praise God's mercy (Homilies on the Gospels II, 20).
magis: Catechism 717–720
John, filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother's womb, is “more than a prophet”; in him the Holy Spirit concludes the speaking through the prophets.
Evangelium Vitae 45
John leaping in his mother's womb shows that human life is a gift from the very beginning, and that God's love reaches the child before birth.
Catechism 2214–2216
The divine fatherhood is the source of human fatherhood; children are a gift, and parents are called to receive and form them.
saints: 6 Dec: St Nicholas. 7 Dec: St Ambrose. 8 Dec: the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Confirm others in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-12-06.prayer: Lord God, you gave Zechariah and Elizabeth a son and named him John, for you are gracious. Loose our tongues to bless you, bless the children you entrust to us, and prepare our hearts for the Dawn from on high, your Son Jesus Christ. Amen.

2026-12-13.title: Sunday of the Apparition of the Angel to St Joseph
readings: The dreams of Joseph, son of Jacob
Turn to me and be saved
Joseph takes Mary as his wife
2026-12-13.verse: Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
theo: Luke told us the story through Mary; Matthew tells it through Joseph. Joseph discovers that Mary, his betrothed, is with child, and he does not yet know how. St Matthew describes him in one word: he was “a righteous man”. His righteousness is shown in mercy: “unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, he planned to dismiss her quietly.”

Then God speaks to him in a dream: “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.” Joseph is given two tasks: to receive Mary and to name the child. By naming him, Joseph gives Jesus his legal place in the house of David.

Joseph never speaks a word in the Gospels. But he acts: “When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took her as his wife.” His obedience is immediate and complete. Like the young Samuel he says, in deeds if not in words, “Speak, for your servant is listening.” The patriarch Joseph, the dreamer of Genesis, saved his family by going down to Egypt; this Joseph will save the Holy Family by taking them to Egypt.

Matthew adds: “All this took place to fulfill what had been spoken by the Lord through the prophet: ‘Look, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall name him Emmanuel,’ which means, ‘God is with us.’” Through Joseph's quiet faith, God-with-us receives a home, a family name and a father's protection.
conn: Two Josephs, two dreamers.
Joseph son of Jacob dreamed and was sent ahead to Egypt to save his family (Genesis 37; 45:5). Joseph of Nazareth dreams and takes the Child to Egypt to save him (Matthew 2:13–15).
Samuel's listening heart.
“Speak, for your servant is listening” (1 Samuel 3:10) describes Joseph exactly: he listens and obeys.
Son of David.
The angel calls Joseph “son of David”. Through Joseph's legal fatherhood, Jesus is heir to the promise made to David (2 Samuel 7:12–16).
Called before birth.
Paul says God “set me apart before I was born and called me through his grace” (Galatians 1:15). Joseph too was chosen in God's plan for a hidden but essential mission.
altar: Joseph received Mary and the Child into his home without fully understanding. At the Holy Qurbono we receive Christ under the humble signs of bread and wine, with the same faith that does not need to see everything in order to trust.
outline: Ask: how do we react when life does not go according to our plan?
Point 1 · A righteous man is merciful
Joseph's righteousness is not harshness but mercy (Matthew 1:19). A word on gossip and protecting others' dignity.
Point 2 · God speaks in the night
Joseph listens in the dream. Do we give God room to speak: silence, prayer, Scripture?
“He did as the angel commanded.” Faith without delay.
Joseph gives a name, a home and protection. A word to fathers and to all who care for others' children.
live: Protect someone's dignity (Matthew 1:19)
Refuse to pass on one piece of gossip this week; speak well of the person instead.
Listen before sleeping (1 Samuel 3:10)
End each day with five minutes of silence, saying: “Speak, Lord, your servant is listening.”
Honour fathers
Pray for the fathers of your family and parish; fathers, bless your children before Christmas.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
Joseph's righteousness, he says, is shown in his gentleness: he wished to spare Mary even the least shame, a sign of true virtue (Homilies on Matthew 4).
St Bernard of Clairvaux
He compares the two Josephs: the first kept bread for Egypt; the second guarded the Living Bread from heaven for the whole world (Homilies in Praise of the Virgin Mother 2, 16).
magis: Redemptoris Custos 3–4
St John Paul II: Joseph's “obedience of faith” parallels Mary's; by taking Mary as his wife he took part in the mystery of the Incarnation.
Patris Corde (2020)
Pope Francis describes Joseph as a beloved, tender, obedient, accepting, creatively courageous and working father, “in the shadow”.
Catechism 437, 497
The angel announced to Joseph the Child conceived by the Holy Spirit; Jesus is the Christ, son of David.
saints: 13 Dec: St Lucy. 14 Dec: St John of the Cross. 18 Dec: the Miraculous Cross of Mylapore (as in the 2025–26 lectionary). Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-12-13.prayer: Lord God, you entrusted your Son and the Virgin Mary to the faithful care of Joseph, the righteous man. Give us his listening heart, his merciful justice and his prompt obedience, and bless all fathers with his tender strength. Amen.

2026-12-20.title: Sunday before Yaldo
readings: Jacob's family goes down to Egypt
God's promise to the house of David
A shoot from the stump of Jesse
In your descendants all families shall be blessed
Joseph and Mary go up to Bethlehem
2026-12-20.alt: Sixth Sunday of Suboro. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was also kept as Bible Sunday. Yaldo falls on Friday 25 December.
2026-12-20.verse: A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots.
theo: On the last Sunday before Yaldo the Church reads names: the long genealogy of Jesus, and the list of Jacob's family going down to Egypt. These lists can seem dry, but they say something essential: God's salvation enters real history, through real families, over many generations.

The prophets used the image of a tree. The royal house of David had been cut down like a stump; but Isaiah says, “A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots.” Jeremiah repeats it: “I will raise up for David a righteous Branch.” When everything seemed dead, God was preparing new life from the old root.

Luke brings the promise to a dusty road. Because of a decree of Caesar Augustus, “Joseph also went from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem… He went to be registered with Mary, to whom he was engaged and who was expecting a child.” The emperor thinks he is counting his subjects; in fact he is bringing the Son of David to the town where the prophet Micah said the ruler of Israel would be born.

Peter in Acts recalls God's word to Abraham: “In your descendants all the families of the earth shall be blessed” (Acts 3:25). The genealogy does not end with Jesus; it continues in us, the Church, who by Baptism are grafted into this family tree. As Yaldo approaches, we prepare not only to remember a birth, but to welcome the Saviour into our own family history.
conn: Down to Egypt, up to Bethlehem.
Jacob's family went down to Egypt with God's promise: “I myself will go down with you” (Genesis 46:4). Now the Son of God comes down into our history, and his family goes up to Bethlehem.
The Spirit on the Branch.
Isaiah 11:2 describes the Spirit resting on the shoot of Jesse, the source of the gifts of the Spirit.
The peaceable kingdom.
“The wolf shall live with the lamb” (Isaiah 11:6): the Child of Bethlehem brings a peace that heals even creation.
A priest from Judah.
Hebrews 7:14 notes that our Lord came from Judah, not Levi: a new priesthood “according to the order of Melchizedek”.
altar: Bethlehem means “house of bread”. The Son of David born there gives himself as the Bread of Life. As we go up to Yaldo, each Holy Qurbono is our journey to Bethlehem.
outline: Ask: do you know the names of your great-grandparents? Why do families keep these names?
The genealogies: saints and sinners, Jews and foreigners. Your family history is not outside God's plan.
Point 2 · New life from a stump
Isaiah 11. When something in our life seems cut down, God can make it sprout.
The emperor's decree serves God's plan. God uses even inconvenient events.
The Word that became flesh speaks to us in Scripture. Practical: keep a Bible open at home.
“My family is part of God's story.”
live: Pray for your family tree
Write the names of your grandparents and great-grandparents and pray for them, living and departed.
Read the Christmas Gospel at home
On Christmas Eve, read Luke 2:1–20 together as a family before the crib.
Finish the Nombu well
Make your Christmas Confession this week and plan one act of charity for Yaldo.
fathers: St Irenaeus of Lyons
Luke traces Christ's genealogy back to Adam to show that Christ “recapitulates” in himself all the nations and generations of humanity, from the beginning (Against Heresies III, 22, 3).
St Ephrem the Syrian
In his Nativity hymns he sings of the Shoot from the root of Jesse, through whom the old trunk of humanity blossoms again (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: Catechism 525–526
Jesus was born in a humble stable in Bethlehem; to become a child in relation to God is the condition for entering the kingdom.
Dei Verbum 25
Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ (St Jerome); the faithful are urged to frequent reading of the divine Scriptures.
Catechism 1213, 1267
By Baptism we become members of the Body of Christ, the family of God.
saints: 25 Dec (Friday): Yaldo, the Nativity of our Lord, Holy Qurbono for the people. 26 Dec: Exaltation of Mary, Mother of God. 27 Dec: Commemoration of the infants killed by Herod (as in the 2025–26 lectionary). Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-12-20.prayer: Lord God, from the stump of Jesse you made a Branch to grow, and through many generations you prepared the birth of your Son. Bless our families and our ancestors, make your Word live in our homes, and lead us like Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, to welcome the Saviour. Amen.

2026-12-25.title: Yaldo · The Nativity of our Lord
readings: The birth of Isaac: God brings laughter
A son promised to the Shunammite woman
From Bethlehem shall come a ruler
For a child has been born for us
God raised up his servant to bless you
2026-12-25.alt: Yaldo, the Nativity of our Lord. Holy Qurbono for the people. The season of Yaldo–Denho begins.
2026-12-25.verse: And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
theo: Tonight and today the Church sings the mystery she has waited for since Qudos Eetho: “The Word became flesh and lived among us.” The eternal Son of the Father, through whom all things were made, becomes a child, born of the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem. God has not sent a message only; he has come himself.

The prophets had seen it from far away. Isaiah: “The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light… For a child has been born for us, a son given to us… and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” Micah: from little Bethlehem shall come one “whose origin is from of old, from ancient days”. The Child is truly man, born in time, and truly God, born of the Father before all ages.

The Old Testament births read today, Isaac to old Sarah and a son to the Shunammite woman, were births of joy against all expectation. Sarah said: “God has brought laughter for me.” In Bethlehem the joy is greater, because this Child is not only a gift of God; he is God the Gift.

In the Malankara lectionary the Gospel of Yaldo is the coming of the Magi. Strangers from the East follow a star, kneel before the Child with Mary his mother, and offer gold, frankincense and myrrh: gold for a king, incense for God, myrrh for one who will die. From the first day, Christ is revealed to the nations. Our ancestors in India received the same faith from the East; today we kneel with the Magi.
conn: The Light in the darkness.
“The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it” (John 1:5) fulfils Isaiah 9:2: the people in darkness have seen a great light.
Bethlehem, the house of bread.
The Child laid in a manger, a feeding trough, will give himself as the Bread of Life (John 6:51).
Kings bring gifts.
Psalm 72:10 and Isaiah 60:3 foresee kings and nations coming to the light of the Lord; the Magi are their first fruits.
A priest for ever.
Hebrews 7: the Child of Judah is the eternal High Priest. The One born in Bethlehem will offer himself on the altar of the Cross.
altar: Every Holy Qurbono is a Yaldo: the Word who became flesh in Mary's womb becomes present on the altar under the signs of bread and wine. The shepherds came to see; the Magi came to adore. We come to receive.
outline: The wait is over: from Qudos Eetho through Suboro to this night.
Not a message, but the Word made flesh. True God and true man.
Isaiah 9 and John 1. Name the darkness people carry tonight: grief, debt, migration, illness.
Christ for all nations. Gold, incense, myrrh: what will I offer?
The manger and the altar: the Bread of Life.
“God is with us; the Light has come.”
live: Bring someone to the Child
Invite one person who is alone this Christmas to your home or table.
Offer your gifts
Give one gift this week to someone who cannot repay you.
Keep the crib
Pray before the crib at home every night until Denho.
fathers: St Ephrem the Syrian
“Blessed is the Child who gladdened Bethlehem today!” In his Nativity hymns he marvels that the Lord of all lies in the arms of Mary, the Ancient of Days a little child (Hymns on the Nativity).
St Leo the Great
“Our Saviour, dearly beloved, was born today: let us rejoice. There is no room for sadness on the birthday of Life… Christian, recognise your dignity” (Sermon 21 on the Nativity).
magis: Catechism 456–460
The Word became flesh to save us, to make us know God's love, to be our model of holiness, and to make us partakers of the divine nature.
Catechism 525–528
Christmas and the Epiphany: Jesus born in poverty, revealed to the shepherds and to the nations.
Admirabile Signum (2019)
Pope Francis on the meaning of the Christmas crib: it shows God's tenderness and invites us to become small.
saints: 26 Dec: the Exaltation of Mary, Mother of God. 27 Dec: Commemoration of the Infants killed by Herod (as in the 2025–26 lectionary).
2026-12-25.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal Word made flesh, born of the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem, we kneel before you with the shepherds and the Magi. Fill our homes with your light, our hearts with your peace, and our lives with your joy. Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace. Amen.

2026-12-27.title: First Sunday after Yaldo
readings: The return from Egypt to Nazareth
The boy Samson grows and the Lord blesses him
Let us go to the house of the Lord
Old and young in the streets of Jerusalem
Christ, faithful as a Son over God's house
The boy Jesus in the Temple
2026-12-27.alt: Season of Yaldo–Denho. Today is also the Commemoration of the Infants killed by Herod (27 December, as in the 2025–26 lectionary).
2026-12-27.verse: Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
theo: Two days after Yaldo the Church turns to the hidden life of the Holy Family. Matthew tells how Joseph, warned in a dream, brought the Child and his mother back from Egypt and “made his home in a town called Nazareth”. Luke shows the family going up each year to Jerusalem for the Passover. The Son of God grows up in an ordinary family, in an ordinary village, keeping the ordinary feasts of his people.

At twelve, Jesus stays behind in the Temple. After three days of anxious searching his parents find him “sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.” Mary says, “Your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety.” Jesus answers: “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” His first recorded words reveal who his true Father is.

And yet, the Gospel says, “he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them.” The eternal Son obeys a carpenter and a village woman. Hebrews says Christ is “faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house”. The family of Nazareth is the school where the Son of God learned to be human: to work, to pray, to obey and to grow “in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor”.

Zechariah's vision of Jerusalem is a picture of a blessed family and city: “Old men and old women shall again sit in the streets… and the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing.” Families where the old are honoured and children are safe and joyful are signs of God's kingdom. Today we also remember the infants killed by Herod: the Church has always honoured them as martyrs, and with them we pray for every threatened child.
conn: Out of Egypt.
Like Israel, and like Joseph son of Jacob, the Child goes down to Egypt and comes up again (Hosea 11:1; Matthew 2:15). He relives his people's story to save it.
Growing in grace.
Samson grew “and the LORD blessed him” (Judges 13:24); Isaac grew and was weaned (Genesis 21:8); Jesus “increased in wisdom and in years” (Luke 2:52).
Going up to the house of the Lord.
Psalm 122, “I was glad when they said to me, Let us go to the house of the LORD”, was a pilgrim song. The Holy Family sang such psalms on the road to Jerusalem.
Mary's heart.
Twice Luke says Mary kept these things in her heart (2:19, 51). She is the first contemplative of the Gospel.
altar: The boy Jesus said he must be in his Father's house. Every Sunday we too are called to our Father's house, the church, to listen and to receive. Families who come to Holy Qurbono together are walking the road of Nazareth to Jerusalem.
outline: Ask parents: have you ever lost a child for a few minutes in a crowd? Recall that fear.
Point 1 · God in an ordinary family
Nazareth: work, prayer, obedience, feasts. Holiness is possible at home.
Jesus' first words: his identity and mission. Teach children that the church is their Father's house.
The Son of God obeyed. Children obey, parents listen, all grow.
Pray for every threatened child: the unborn, the abused, children of war.
live: Pray together as a family
Choose one fixed time for family prayer every day this week, even ten minutes.
Bring children to the Father's house
Come to Holy Qurbono as a family, sitting together, and talk about the Gospel on the way home.
Honour the elderly (Zechariah 8:4)
Visit or call grandparents and older relatives during this Christmas season.
fathers: St Ambrose of Milan

He notes that Jesus, at twelve, shows his divinity in the Temple and his humanity in submitting to his parents: the One who is Lord of all becomes subject out of love (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke 2).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He sings of the Child of Nazareth who grew in the house of Joseph, the Son of the Most High obeying a carpenter, and of Mary who was mother and disciple at once (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: Catechism 531–534

The hidden life at Nazareth: Jesus shares the condition of the vast majority of people, a daily life of manual work, obedience and prayer; the finding in the Temple reveals his total consecration to the Father.
Amoris Laetitia 65–66
The Holy Family of Nazareth is a model and a light for every family; the covenant of love is lived in daily life.
Catechism 1655–1666
The Christian family as the domestic Church.
saints: 27 Dec: Commemoration of the Infants killed by Herod. 1 Jan: Naming of our Lord; New Year. 2 Jan: Mar Baselios and Mar Gregory, name day of our Major Archbishop-Catholicos Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis. 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-12-27.prayer: Lord Jesus, you grew up in the home of Mary and Joseph at Nazareth, obedient to them and busy with your Father's affairs. Bless our families: make our homes places of prayer, work and love, protect every child, and honour every elder. Amen.

2026-12-01.title: Tuesday after the Sunday of the Visitation · The Twenty-Five Days' Fast begins
readings: Put on the Lord Jesus Christ
The light shines in the darkness
2026-12-01.alt: The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo (Christmas), 1–24 December: prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
2026-12-01.verse: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
theo: The fast begins with the prologue of John: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The child we await at Yaldo is not merely a good man born long ago; he is the eternal Word through whom all things were made, the life that is the light of all people. “The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.” Our fasting is a way of opening the windows to that light.

Paul gives the programme for these twenty-five days. Owe no one anything except love, for love is the fulfilling of the law. “The night is far gone, the day is near. Let us then lay aside the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.” No reveling and drunkenness, no quarrelling and jealousy; instead, “put on the Lord Jesus Christ.” A fast without love is only a diet; a fast with love prepares a home for Christ.
outline: Why do we fast before Christmas?
Owe no one anything but love.
Point 2 · Wake up, the day is near
Put on the armour of light.
Point 3 · The Word and the light
live: Fast with love (Romans 13:8)
Join your fast to one act of love each day.
Lay aside darkness (Romans 13:12)
Give up one habit of the night: late screens, gossip, or anger.
2026-12-01.prayer: Eternal Word, light that the darkness cannot overcome, as we begin this fast, help us lay aside the works of darkness, put on the armour of light, and clothe ourselves with you. Amen.
altar: The fast leads us to the Holy Qurbono of Yaldo. At each Qurbono in these days, the Word who shines in the darkness comes to us as food for the journey.

2026-12-02.title: Wednesday after the Sunday of the Visitation
readings: How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news
Let your word be Yes or No
2026-12-02.alt: The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo (Christmas), 1–24 December: prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
2026-12-02.verse: And how are they to proclaim him unless they are sent? As it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
theo: Paul builds a chain: people cannot call on one they have not believed in, cannot believe in one they have not heard of, cannot hear without a preacher, and there are no preachers unless they are sent. So the Church sends, and the feet of those who bring good news are beautiful. In this season before Christmas, every Christian is sent to announce that the Saviour comes.

Jesus asks for a simple, truthful tongue. Do not swear by heaven or earth or Jerusalem or your own head. “Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.” The messenger of the Word made flesh must be a person whose word can be trusted. Our fasting purifies the tongue as well as the stomach.
outline: “Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’.”
live: Fast from lies (Matthew 5:37)
Speak only the truth today, even in small things.
Be sent (Romans 10:15)
Share one sentence of faith with someone this week.
2026-12-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, you send us to bring good news. Purify our tongues, make our yes and no truthful, and make our feet beautiful on the mountains of this world. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we hear the good news proclaimed. We receive the Word made flesh, and are sent out with beautiful feet.

2026-12-03.title: Thursday after the Sunday of the Visitation · St Francis Xavier
2026-12-03.alt: St Francis Xavier, Jesuit priest and missionary (died 1552). He arrived in Goa in 1542 and preached along the coasts of South India, including Travancore, before going on to the Malay world and Japan (History). His body rests in Goa. The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo (Christmas), 1–24 December: prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
2026-12-03.verse: And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.
theo: Paul, free in Christ, made himself a slave to all in order to win more of them: a Jew to the Jews, weak to the weak. “I have become all things to all people, that I might by all means save some.” This is the missionary's freedom: not changing the gospel, but changing himself, his comfort, his language and his habits, so that others can receive it.

The risen Lord rebukes the Eleven for their unbelief and then sends them anyway: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.” St Francis Xavier took those words to the letter. Sailing from Lisbon, he arrived in Goa in 1542, walked the fishing villages of South India, including the coast of Travancore, then went on to the Malay world and Japan. He died on an island off the coast of China, longing to enter it.
outline: How far would you go for the Gospel?
Point 2 · Go into all the world
The mandate of the risen Lord.
“Go into all the world and proclaim the good news.”
live: Pray for missionaries (Mark 16:15)
Pray for one missionary priest or sister from your parish or eparchy.
Meet someone where they are (1 Corinthians 9:22)
Listen patiently to someone very different from you.
2026-12-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, you sent your apostles into all the world. Through the prayers of St Francis Xavier, who preached on our shores, give us his zeal, his humility, and his love for all peoples. Amen.
altar: At the end of the Holy Qurbono we are sent. Like the apostles, we go out to proclaim the good news by our lives.

2026-12-04.title: Friday after the Sunday of the Visitation · St John of Damascus
readings: Faith comes from what is heard
2026-12-04.alt: Mar Yohannan of Damascus (St John Damascene), monk of the Lavra of St Sabbas near Jerusalem, defender of holy icons, died around 749; Doctor of the Church. The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo (Christmas), 1–24 December: prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
2026-12-04.verse: leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.
theo: “So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.” Paul quotes Isaiah: God let himself be found by those who did not seek him. The word has gone out to the ends of the earth. St John of Damascus, whom we remember today, spent his life handing on that word faithfully; he also defended the holy icons, teaching that because the invisible God became visible in Christ, his face may be painted and venerated.

Jesus goes beneath the commandment “You shall not murder” to its root: anger and contempt. Whoever is angry with a brother or calls him a fool is already on the road to murder. And then a teaching for every worshipper: if at the altar you remember that your brother has something against you, “leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled”. Our offering at the Holy Qurbono is not acceptable while we refuse to be reconciled. A Friday of the fast is a good day to make peace.
outline: Is there anyone I need to make peace with before Christmas?
Jesus heals the heart, not only the hand.
The word reaches even those who did not seek.
“First be reconciled to your brother or sister.”
live: Make peace (Matthew 5:24)
Take one step today toward reconciliation.
Venerate an icon (St John Damascene)
Pray before an icon of Christ or the Mother of God at home.
2026-12-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, you call us to be reconciled before we bring our gifts. Heal our anger, give us courage to make peace, and through the prayers of St John of Damascus, let us see your face. Amen.
altar: Before the anaphora we give the peace to one another. Reconciled, we offer the gifts and receive the Lord.

2026-12-05.title: Saturday after the Sunday of the Visitation · Mar Saba; St Clement of Alexandria
readings: Never has anyone spoken like this
2026-12-05.alt: Mar Saba (St Sabbas), founder of the Great Lavra in the Judean desert (died 532), and Mar Clement of Alexandria, early Christian teacher (died around 215). The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo (Christmas), 1–24 December: prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
2026-12-05.verse: The police answered, “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
theo: Paul tells Timothy to have nothing to do with silly myths and to “train yourself in godliness”. Physical training has some value, but godliness is valuable in every way, “holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.” That is what a fast is: spiritual training. Mar Saba, whom the East remembers today, trained himself for decades in the desert and founded a monastery that still stands near Jerusalem.

The temple police were sent to arrest Jesus and came back empty-handed. Asked why, they could only say: “Never has anyone spoken like this!” The crowds argue whether he is the prophet or the Messiah; the leaders sneer that no prophet comes from Galilee. Only Nicodemus asks for a fair hearing. In this fast, let us give Jesus that fair hearing, listening to his word until, like the police, we are disarmed by it.
outline: Point 2 · Hope in the living God
Point 3 · Never has anyone spoken like this
live: Spiritual exercise (1 Timothy 4:7)
Add five minutes of silent prayer to each day of the fast.
Give Jesus a hearing (John 7:51)
Read one chapter of a Gospel today without hurry.
2026-12-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, no one has ever spoken as you speak. Train us in godliness during this fast, set our hope on the living God, and through the prayers of Mar Saba, let your word disarm our hearts. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we hear the words of the One who spoke like no one else, and receive him as the bread of eternal life.

2026-12-07.title: Monday after the Sunday of the Birth of John the Baptist · St Ambrose
readings: Take courage; I have conquered the world
2026-12-07.alt: St Ambrose, Bishop of Milan (died 397), Doctor of the Church, who baptised St Augustine. The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-07.verse: I have said this to you, so that in me you may have peace. In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!
theo: From prison Paul tells Timothy not to be ashamed of the testimony about the Lord, and gives his own reason: “I know the one in whom I have put my trust.” Christ has abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel. Timothy's task is to “guard the good treasure entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit living in us.” St Ambrose did just that in Milan: he guarded the faith against error and handed it on, among others to a restless young teacher named Augustine.

On the night before he died Jesus speaks plainly to his disciples: the Father himself loves you. They will soon be scattered and leave him alone, “yet I am not alone because the Father is with me.” Then a word for every anxious heart: “In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!” The peace of Christ is not the absence of trouble; it is his victory present in the middle of it.
outline: I know whom I have believed.
Hand on the faith with the Spirit's help.
“Take courage; I have conquered the world!”
live: Witness without shame (2 Timothy 1:8)
Make the sign of the cross before eating in public today.
Bring your fear to Christ (John 16:33)
Name one fear in prayer and say: Jesus, you have conquered it.
2026-12-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, you have conquered the world. Give us your peace in every trouble, courage to witness without shame, and, through the prayers of St Ambrose, the grace to guard and hand on the faith. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we receive the One who has conquered the world. In him we find courage.

2026-12-08.title: The Immaculate Conception of the Holy Mother of God
readings: God sent his Son, born of a woman
2026-12-08.alt: Feast of the Immaculate Conception. The Catholic Church professes that Mary, by a singular grace of God and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ, was preserved free from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception (Pope Pius IX, Ineffabilis Deus, 1854; Catechism 491). The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-08.verse: for the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.
theo: “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman.” To prepare a worthy mother for his Son, God filled Mary with grace from the very first moment of her existence. The Church professes that she was preserved from every stain of original sin, not by her own merit, but “in view of the merits of Jesus Christ, the Saviour of the human race” (Ineffabilis Deus, 1854). She too was redeemed by her Son, in the most perfect way: preserved rather than cleansed.

In the Magnificat Mary herself gives the reason for today's feast: “the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.” She does not boast of her purity; she praises God's mercy. In Genesis God had promised enmity between the serpent and the woman; in Mary that promise begins to be fulfilled. Through her Son we too become children and heirs, able to cry “Abba! Father!”, and in the middle of the Christmas fast we look to her as the pure dwelling God prepared for his coming.
outline: What does it mean to be full of grace?
God prepares a mother for his Son.
The first fruit of Christ's redemption.
Point 3 · The Mighty One has done great things
live: Pray the Magnificat (Luke 1:46–55)
Pray Mary's song slowly today.
Make room for grace (Galatians 4:6)
Make a good confession before Yaldo.
2026-12-08.prayer: All-holy God, you prepared a worthy dwelling for your Son by preserving the Virgin Mary from every stain of sin. By her prayers, purify our hearts, so that we too may welcome your Son at his coming. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we receive the Body born of the pure Virgin. With her, our souls magnify the Lord.

2026-12-09.title: Wednesday after the Sunday of the Birth of John the Baptist
readings: God has spoken to us by a Son
Are you the one who is to come?
2026-12-09.alt: The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-09.verse: And he answered them, “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised,
theo: Hebrews opens with a sweeping vision: “Long ago God spoke to our ancestors in many and various ways by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son,” through whom he made the worlds. The Son is “the reflection of God's glory and the exact imprint of God's very being”; having made purification for sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high. The child of Bethlehem is God's final and complete Word.

John the Baptist, in prison, sends disciples to ask Jesus: “Are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another?” Jesus does not answer with a title but with signs: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor hear good news, all fulfilling Isaiah. “And blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me.” Even great saints have dark hours; Jesus answers them with his works.
outline: Have you ever asked God: are you really there?
Point 1 · God has spoken in his Son
Point 3 · Blessed who take no offence
“Go and tell John what you have seen and heard.”
live: Bring your question (Luke 7:19)
Tell Jesus honestly one doubt or question you carry.
Look for his works (Luke 7:22)
Write down three things God has done for you this year.
2026-12-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, Son through whom the Father speaks, you answered John's doubt with signs of mercy. Answer our questions, open our eyes to your works, and keep us from taking offence at your ways. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono God speaks by the Son, and then gives us the Son himself as food.

2026-12-10.title: Thursday after the Sunday of the Birth of John the Baptist · Mar Behnam, his sister Sarah and the Forty Martyrs
readings: Taught by God to love one another
2026-12-10.alt: Mar Behnam and his sister Sarah, with forty companions, martyrs honoured especially in the Syriac Churches (4th century; their story comes from Tradition and contains legendary elements). The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-10.verse: Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven;
theo: Jesus prepares his disciples for persecution with three times “Do not be afraid.” What is whispered will be proclaimed from the housetops. Do not fear those who can kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Not one sparrow falls to the ground apart from the Father; even the hairs of your head are counted; “you are of more value than many sparrows.” And the promise: whoever acknowledges me before others, I will acknowledge before my Father. The Syriac Churches today remember Mar Behnam and his sister Sarah, honoured as martyrs who acknowledged Christ before others.

Paul's advice to the Thessalonians is quieter but no less demanding: they have been “taught by God to love one another”; let them do so more and more, aspire to live quietly, mind their own affairs and work with their hands. Ordinary faithfulness, lived day after day, is also a kind of witness; it prepares the heart for the extraordinary moment when courage is required.
outline: “Everyone who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge.”
live: Acknowledge Christ (Matthew 10:32)
Say grace openly at your next meal with others.
Love more and more (1 Thessalonians 4:10)
Do one hidden act of love for a family member.
2026-12-10.prayer: Lord Jesus, you tell us not to be afraid. Through the prayers of Mar Behnam, Sarah and the holy martyrs, give us courage to acknowledge you before others and faithfulness in love day after day. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the Father, who cares for every sparrow, feeds his children with the Body and Blood of his Son.

2026-12-11.title: Friday after the Sunday of the Birth of John the Baptist
readings: The Son of Man is lord of the sabbath
2026-12-11.alt: The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-11.verse: For the Son of Man is lord of the sabbath.
theo: Paul organises a collection for the poor Christians of Jerusalem and gives a simple method: “On the first day of every week, each of you is to put aside and save whatever extra you earn.” The first day of the week is Sunday, the day of the Resurrection. From the beginning, the Lord's Day and care for the poor went together; the offering at the Holy Qurbono is a continuation of that collection.

When the hungry disciples pluck grain on the sabbath, the Pharisees object. Jesus reminds them that David ate the holy bread when he was hungry, and that the priests work in the temple on the sabbath. “I tell you, something greater than the temple is here… ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice.’” Jesus is not abolishing the holy day; he is its Lord, and he shows that its holiness is fulfilled in mercy. In this fast, our self-denial should become mercy for the hungry.
outline: What does Sunday mean in our home?
Point 1 · The first day of the week
The Lord's Day and the poor.
“The Son of Man is lord of the sabbath.”
live: Set aside for the poor (1 Corinthians 16:2)
Put aside the money saved by fasting for the poor.
Keep Sunday holy (Matthew 12:8)
Plan next Sunday around the Qurbono, family and rest.
2026-12-11.prayer: Lord Jesus, Lord of the sabbath, teach us to keep your day holy by worship and by mercy. Let what we save by fasting feed the hungry, and let our sacrifice always be joined to love. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we offer the sacrifice that God desires, joined to Christ's own merciful love.

2026-12-12.title: Saturday after the Sunday of the Birth of John the Baptist
2026-12-12.alt: The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-12.verse: Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
theo: Paul ends his first letter with a burst of short commands, like a spiritual rule of life: respect those who labour among you; be at peace; admonish the idle, encourage the faint-hearted, help the weak; do not repay evil for evil. “Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.” Do not quench the Spirit; test everything; hold fast to what is good.

Jesus speaks with startling seriousness about sin: better to lose a hand, a foot or an eye than to be thrown into the fire. He does not mean self-mutilation, but radical decisiveness: cut off whatever leads you or a little one into sin. Then a gentle image: “Salt is good… Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.” Salt preserves and gives flavour; in the Old Testament every offering was seasoned with “the salt of the covenant”. Our fast is a season to become salt again.
outline: What gives flavour to a Christian life?
Point 2 · Cut off what causes sin
Be at peace with one another.
“Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
live: Pray without ceasing (1 Thessalonians 5:17)
Repeat a short prayer like “Lord Jesus, have mercy on me” throughout the day.
Cut off one occasion of sin (Mark 9:43)
Delete or remove one thing that regularly leads you into sin.
2026-12-12.prayer: Lord Jesus, teach us to rejoice always, pray without ceasing and give thanks in all things. Give us courage to cut away what leads us into sin, and make us salt that brings peace. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono is the great thanksgiving. Here we rejoice, pray and give thanks with Christ.

2026-12-14.title: Monday after the Sunday of the Apparition to St Joseph · St John of the Cross
readings: Carry the cross and count the cost
2026-12-14.alt: St John of the Cross, Carmelite friar and mystic (died 1591), Doctor of the Church; Mar Abraham Kidunaya, Syrian hermit (Tradition). The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-14.verse: Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
theo: Hebrews meditates on a mysterious figure: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, who blessed Abraham and received a tenth of everything. His name means “king of righteousness” and Salem means “peace”. With no recorded father or mother, no beginning or end, “resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.” Genesis says he brought out bread and wine; the Fathers saw in him a sign of Christ, the eternal Priest who offers himself under bread and wine.

Jesus turns to the crowds following him and tells them the cost of discipleship: to put him before every family tie, even before one's own life; to carry the cross; to sit down and count the cost like a builder or a king going to war. “None of you can become my disciple if you do not give up all your possessions.” St John of the Cross lived this in the dark night of prison and wrote some of the most beautiful poetry of love for God. The way of the cross leads to the light of Christmas and of Easter.
outline: What does following Jesus cost you?
“Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.”
live: Accept today's cross (Luke 14:27)
Bear one difficulty today without complaining, for love of Christ.
Finish what you began (Luke 14:28)
Complete one good resolution you made at the start of the fast.
2026-12-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, eternal Priest after the order of Melchizedek, give us courage to carry our cross and follow you, and through the prayers of St John of the Cross, lead us through every dark night into your light. Amen.
altar: Christ, priest for ever according to the order of Melchizedek, offers himself to the Father under the signs of bread and wine, and gives himself to us.

2026-12-15.title: Tuesday after the Sunday of the Apparition to St Joseph
2026-12-15.alt: The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-15.verse: For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
theo: Paul came to Corinth, a city proud of rhetoric and philosophy, “in weakness and in fear and in much trembling.” He did not try to impress them: “I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.” His preaching was not plausible words of wisdom but “a demonstration of the Spirit and of power, so that your faith might rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God.” The crib and the cross are both foolishness to the world and power to those who believe.

Jesus warns his disciples of what lies ahead: they will be put out of the synagogues; some will even think that killing them is an offering to God. “I have said these things to you to keep you from stumbling.” Forewarned is forearmed. Christmas is not a sentimental holiday; the child of Bethlehem will be rejected, and those who follow him will share his rejection, and his victory.
outline: Point 3 · So that you may not stumble
live: Look at the cross (1 Corinthians 2:2)
Pray five minutes before a crucifix today.
Stand firm (John 16:1)
Pray for Christians who face exclusion for their faith.
2026-12-15.prayer: Lord Jesus, crucified and risen, be the centre of our faith. Free us from relying on human cleverness, let our faith rest on the power of God, and keep us from stumbling when trials come. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we proclaim Christ crucified. His weakness on the cross is the power of God that saves us.

2026-12-16.title: Wednesday after the Sunday of the Apparition to St Joseph
readings: My grace is sufficient for you
Who do you say that I am?
2026-12-16.alt: Anniversary of the erection of the Eparchy of Marthandom (1996). The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-16.verse: but he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.” So, I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
theo: Jesus, after praying alone, asks his disciples two questions. First: “Who do the crowds say that I am?” They answer: John the Baptist, Elijah, one of the ancient prophets. Then the decisive one: “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answers, “The Messiah of God.” Opinions about Jesus are many; each of us must give our own answer. Christmas puts the same question to every person who looks at the child in the manger.

Paul tells of “a thorn in the flesh” that he begged the Lord three times to remove. The answer was not removal but grace: “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.” So Paul boasts of his weaknesses, “for whenever I am weak, then I am strong.” God chose to come to us as a weak infant; he still meets us in our weakness, not only in our strength.
outline: What do people say about Jesus today?
Point 1 · Who do you say I am?
The power of the child of Bethlehem.
live: Answer the question (Luke 9:20)
Write in one sentence who Jesus is for you.
Offer your thorn (2 Corinthians 12:8)
Bring one persistent weakness to the Lord and ask for his grace.
2026-12-16.prayer: Lord Jesus, Messiah of God, we confess you as our Lord. When our thorns remain, let your grace be enough for us, and let your power be made perfect in our weakness. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we confess Christ as the Messiah of God and receive the grace that is sufficient for us.

2026-12-17.title: Thursday after the Sunday of the Apparition to St Joseph · Mar Rabbula
readings: The God of peace will crush Satan
You will know them by their fruits
2026-12-17.alt: Mar Rabbula, Bishop of Edessa (died around 436), remembered in the Syriac tradition. The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-17.verse: Thus you will know them by their fruits.
theo: At the end of Romans Paul warns against those who cause dissensions and offences, serving “their own appetites” and deceiving the simple with smooth talk. He wants the Romans to be “wise in what is good and guileless in what is evil.” And then a promise that echoes Genesis: “The God of peace will shortly crush Satan under your feet.” The child born of the woman will strike the serpent's head; his victory becomes ours.

Jesus warns against false prophets who come in sheep's clothing. How do we recognise them? Not by their eloquence or their claims, but by their fruits: a good tree bears good fruit, a bad tree bad fruit. “Thus you will know them by their fruits.” The same test applies to us. In these last days of the fast we ask whether our lives bear the fruits of Christ: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness.
outline: How do you recognise a true teacher?
Point 2 · Wise in what is good
“You will know them by their fruits.”
live: Test the voices (Matthew 7:15)
Before sharing religious content online, check whether it is faithful to the Church.
Bear good fruit (Matthew 7:17)
Do one act of kindness to someone who irritates you.
2026-12-17.prayer: God of peace, crush the power of evil under our feet. Give us wisdom to know the true from the false, and make our lives good trees bearing the fruit of your Son. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we receive the true fruit of the tree of life, Christ himself, who makes us good trees.

2026-12-18.title: Friday after the Sunday of the Apparition to St Joseph · The Miraculous Cross of Mylapore
readings: I am the way, and the truth, and the life
2026-12-18.alt: Commemoration of the Miraculous Cross of Mylapore: an ancient stone cross with a Pahlavi inscription found at St Thomas Mount, Chennai, in the sixteenth century (History); the account that it sweated on 18 December 1558 comes from Tradition. The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-18.verse: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
theo: Paul calls himself “the very least of all the saints”, yet to him was given the grace “to bring to the Gentiles the news of the boundless riches of Christ”, the mystery hidden for ages in God. Through the Church the manifold wisdom of God is now made known. The ancient cross venerated at St Thomas Mount in Mylapore is a witness that these riches reached our land early: Christians in India carved the sign of the cross long before the Portuguese arrived.

On the eve of his passion Jesus tells his troubled disciples: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me. In my Father's house there are many dwelling places.” When Thomas, the apostle of India, asks, “How can we know the way?”, Jesus answers with one of the greatest sayings of the Gospel: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.” The cross is the way he walked to prepare a place for us.
outline: What troubles your heart this Christmas?
Point 3 · The boundless riches of Christ
“I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”
live: Trust (John 14:1)
Hand over one troubling worry to Jesus today.
Venerate the cross (Ephesians 3:8)
Kiss or bow before the cross in your home tonight.
2026-12-18.prayer: Lord Jesus, way, truth and life, calm our troubled hearts. Through the prayers of St Thomas the Apostle, who asked you the way, lead us by your cross to the Father's house. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the boundless riches of Christ are given to us. He who is the way becomes our food for the journey.

2026-12-19.title: Saturday after the Sunday of the Apparition to St Joseph
readings: Go and tell John what you hear and see
2026-12-19.alt: Tomorrow is the Sunday before Yaldo and Bible Sunday. The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-19.verse: in whom you also are built together spiritually into a dwelling place for God.
theo: On the last Saturday before Christmas the Church reads again Paul's vision of reconciliation: Christ is our peace; he has broken down the dividing wall and made the far and the near one people, “so he came and proclaimed peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near.” In him the whole structure grows into a holy temple, and we are “built together spiritually into a dwelling place for God.” The God who will lie in a manger wants to dwell in a people.

John, in prison, sends to ask if Jesus is the one who is to come. Jesus answers by pointing to what is happening: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news brought to them. Isaiah had promised that on that day the deaf would hear and the eyes of the blind would see. The kingdom has begun; Christmas is the arrival of the one who heals.
outline: Where does God want to live?
Point 1 · A dwelling place for God
Point 2 · Peace to the far and the near
“Built together into a dwelling place for God.”
live: Prepare a dwelling (Ephesians 2:22)
Clean and decorate your home's prayer corner for Yaldo.
Go and tell (Matthew 11:4)
Tell someone one thing Jesus has done for you.
2026-12-19.prayer: Lord Jesus, you come to make your dwelling among us. Build us into your temple, bring peace to those far and near, and open our eyes and ears to the signs of your coming. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we become one body in Christ. The dividing walls fall at the one table.

2026-12-21.title: Monday after the Sunday before Yaldo
readings: Your faith is proclaimed throughout the world
In him was life, and the life was light
2026-12-21.alt: Season of Yaldo and Denho. The last days of the Twenty-Five Days' Fast.
2026-12-21.verse: All things came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being. What has come into being in him was life, and the life was the light of all people.
theo: Paul begins his letter to the Romans with thanksgiving: “your faith is proclaimed throughout the world.” He longs to visit them, not only to give but to receive: “so that we may be mutually encouraged by each other's faith, both yours and mine.” He feels himself a debtor to everyone, Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish. Faith is never private property; it is a gift we owe to others.

In these last days before Yaldo the Church reads the prologue of John slowly, a few verses each day. Today: “All things came into being through him… What has come into being in him was life, and the life was the light of all people.” The child of Bethlehem is the one through whom the stars and the shepherds and the ox and the ass were made. The Creator enters his own creation as a creature.
outline: Whose faith has encouraged you this year?
A gift to share with the world.
“The life was the light of all people.”
live: Encourage someone's faith (Romans 1:12)
Send a Christmas message that speaks of Jesus, not only of the holidays.
Wonder at creation (John 1:3)
Look at the night sky tonight and thank the Word through whom it was made.
2026-12-21.prayer: Eternal Word, through whom all things were made, you come to us as light and life. Let our faith encourage others, and let us welcome you with wonder at your coming. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the eternal Word, through whom all things were made, comes to us. We share in his life and light.

2026-12-22.title: Tuesday after the Sunday before Yaldo
readings: The true light was coming into the world
2026-12-22.alt: Season of Yaldo and Denho. The last days of the Twenty-Five Days' Fast.
2026-12-22.verse: The true light, which enlightens everyone, was coming into the world.
theo: The prologue introduces a man: “There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. He came as a witness to testify to the light.” John was not the light; he pointed to it. Every Christian has the same vocation: not to be the light but to bear witness to it, so that others may believe. “The true light, which enlightens everyone, was coming into the world.” No one is excluded from its rays.

Paul is distressed that the Galatians, after coming to know God, “or rather to be known by God”, want to go back to the old elemental spirits and anxious observances of days and seasons. Faith is not first our knowing God but God knowing us, loving us before we loved him. Christmas is the feast of being known: God knows our name and comes to find us.
outline: Who pointed you toward the light?
Point 1 · A witness to the light

2026-12-23.title: Wednesday after the Sunday before Yaldo
readings: All the treasures of wisdom in Christ
He gave power to become children of God
2026-12-23.alt: Season of Yaldo and Denho. The last days of the Twenty-Five Days' Fast.
2026-12-23.verse: But to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God,
theo: The prologue now speaks of rejection and welcome. “He was in the world, and the world came into being through him; yet the world did not know him. He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him.” There was no room at the inn. But to all who did receive him, “who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God”, born not of blood or of human will, but of God. Christmas is God's offer of adoption.

Paul struggles in prayer for the Colossians and for many he has never met, so that their hearts may be encouraged and united in love, and that they may have “the knowledge of God's mystery, that is, Christ himself, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” The child in the manger looks poor, but in him are all the treasures of God.
outline: Is there room for Jesus in our house?
Point 1 · His own did not accept him
Point 2 · Power to become children of God
The poor child is God's wealth.
“He gave power to become children of God.”
live: Make room (John 1:11)
Make room in your Christmas plans for someone who would otherwise be alone.
Thank God for adoption (John 1:12)
Renew your baptismal promises in prayer tonight.
2026-12-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came to your own and they did not receive you. We welcome you now: make room in our hearts and homes, make us children of God, and show us all the treasures hidden in you. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we receive him, and he gives us the power to become children of God.

2026-12-24.title: Thursday after the Sunday before Yaldo · Eve of Yaldo
readings: God's power seen in what he has made
2026-12-24.alt: Eve of Yaldo (Christmas). The Twenty-Five Days' Fast ends with the festal Holy Qurbono of Yaldo.
2026-12-24.verse: And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
theo: On the eve of Yaldo the prologue reaches its summit: “And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory.” The Greek says he “pitched his tent” among us, like the tabernacle in the desert filled with God's glory. From his fullness we have all received “grace upon grace”. The law came through Moses; grace and truth through Jesus Christ. “No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, who has made him known.”

Paul's words to the Romans are sobering: God's eternal power and divine nature have been visible in creation from the beginning, yet human beings exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal things. Christmas is God's answer to our idolatry: no longer an image made by human hands, but the true Image of God, born of a woman, lying in a manger. Tonight the whole Church kneels before him.
outline: What would you prepare if God came to stay at your house?
God pitches his tent among us.
“The Word became flesh and lived among us.”
live: Prepare your heart (John 1:14)
If possible, make your confession today and come to the Yaldo Qurbono.
Leave the idols (Romans 1:23)
Let the gifts and food tomorrow be at the service of Christ, not the centre.
2026-12-24.prayer: Word made flesh, you pitched your tent among us and showed us the Father's glory. As we keep the vigil of your birth, fill us with grace upon grace, and make our hearts a fitting dwelling for you. Amen.
altar: Tonight at the Holy Qurbono the Word made flesh is given to us. From his fullness we receive grace upon grace.

2026-12-26.title: The Praise of the Holy Mother of God
readings: God sent his Son, born of a woman
2026-12-26.alt: On the day after Yaldo the Syriac Churches praise the Mother of God, who gave birth to the Saviour. Season of Yaldo and Denho.
2026-12-26.verse: But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
theo: The day after Christmas the Syriac tradition turns to the one through whom the Word took flesh. “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman.” Mary is not a decoration of the feast but the human door through which God entered history. Because she said yes, “God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, ‘Abba! Father!’” and we are no longer slaves but children and heirs.

The shepherds hurry to Bethlehem and find Mary and Joseph and the child lying in the manger. They tell everyone what the angels said, and all who hear are amazed. “But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.” The crowd is amazed for a moment; Mary keeps and ponders for a lifetime. She is the model of every believer who wants Christmas to last beyond one day.
outline: What do we keep from Christmas when the decorations come down?
Mary, the door of God's coming.
“Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.”
live: Ponder with Mary (Luke 2:19)
Sit before the crib for ten minutes in silence today.
Tell what you have seen (Luke 2:17)
Share with someone one way Christmas touched you.
2026-12-26.prayer: Holy Mother of God, through you the Word took flesh. Teach us to treasure and ponder the mystery of your Son, as the shepherds hurry to see him and the angels sing his glory. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we receive the Body born of the Mother of God, and with her we treasure the mystery in our hearts.

2026-12-28.title: Monday after the First Sunday after Yaldo · David, King and Prophet
2026-12-28.alt: Commemoration of David, King and Prophet. Season of Yaldo and Denho.
2026-12-28.verse: “What do you think of the Messiah? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “The son of David.”
theo: Three days after Christmas the Church remembers David, the shepherd boy of Bethlehem who became king, poet and prophet. God promised him a house and a throne forever. Jesus, born in David's town, asks the Pharisees: “What do you think of the Messiah? Whose son is he?” They answer, “The son of David.” Then he quotes Psalm 110, where David calls the Messiah “my Lord”. How can he be both David's son and David's Lord? Only if he is the eternal Son of God who became David's descendant. The mystery of Christmas is hidden in that question.

Hebrews lists the heroes of faith, among them David, “who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions.” Others suffered mockery, chains and death. “Yet all these, though they were commended for their faith, did not receive what was promised”: they were waiting for Christ, and for us. The child of Bethlehem fulfils all their hopes.
outline: What do you think of Jesus?
Son of God and son of David.
They waited for what we have received.
“What do you think of the Messiah?”
live: Pray a psalm of David (Psalm 23)
Pray Psalm 23 slowly today.
Face your giant (1 Samuel 17:45)
Bring one great difficulty to God in the name of the Lord.
2026-12-28.prayer: Lord Jesus, Son of David and David's Lord, you fulfil every promise made to the fathers. Give us David's faith and his love for prayer, and keep us faithful until we receive all you have promised. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we greet the Son of David who is our Lord, and pray with a contrite heart for his mercy.

2026-12-29.title: Tuesday after the First Sunday after Yaldo
readings: Honouring God with lips, not hearts
2026-12-29.verse: For God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all.
theo: Paul unveils a mystery: a hardening has come upon part of Israel until the full number of the Gentiles has come in, “and so all Israel will be saved.” God has not rejected his first people: “the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.” In the end everything is mercy: “God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all.” The child born in Bethlehem is the Messiah of Israel and the Saviour of the nations; no one is outside the reach of that mercy.

The Pharisees accuse Jesus' disciples of breaking the tradition of the elders by not washing their hands. Jesus answers that they themselves break God's commandment for the sake of their tradition, for example by using a religious vow to avoid supporting their parents. He quotes Isaiah: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.” In the joy of Christmas, God asks for our hearts, not only our customs.
outline: Is our Christmas more custom or more heart?
God never takes back his call.
No one is beyond his reach.
“God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all.”
live: Honour parents in deed (Matthew 15:4)
Do something concrete for your parents or elders this week.
Pray with the heart (Matthew 15:8)
At the next prayer, slow down and mean each word.
2026-12-29.prayer: Merciful Father, your gifts and your call are irrevocable, and your mercy embraces all. Turn our hearts, not only our lips, to you, and let our Christmas customs express true love for you and for our neighbours. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we honour God with our lips and, by his grace, with our hearts. His mercy is for all.

2026-12-30.title: Wednesday after the First Sunday after Yaldo
readings: He will be called a Nazorean
2026-12-30.verse: May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
theo: After Herod's death an angel tells Joseph in a dream to return with the child and his mother to the land of Israel. Fearing Herod's son Archelaus, he settles in Galilee, in Nazareth, “so that what had been spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled, ‘He will be called a Nazorean.’” Like Israel, the child is called out of Egypt; like a hidden shoot, he grows up in an obscure village. Joseph's quiet obedience protects the life of the Saviour.

Paul tells Jews and Gentiles in Rome: “Welcome one another, therefore, just as Christ has welcomed you, for the glory of God.” Christ became a servant to Israel to confirm the promises, and the Gentiles glorify God for his mercy; Isaiah's “root of Jesse” rises to rule the nations, “in him the Gentiles shall hope.” At the end of the year, Paul's blessing is perfect: “May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing.”
outline: Who needs our welcome as the year ends?
“May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace.”
live: Welcome a stranger (Romans 15:7)
Welcome a migrant or newcomer in your parish or neighbourhood.
Obey quietly (Matthew 2:21)
Do one duty today promptly, like Joseph.
2026-12-30.prayer: God of hope, you brought your Son out of Egypt and hid him in Nazareth. Fill us with joy and peace in believing, teach us to welcome one another as Christ welcomed us, and make us abound in hope by the power of your Spirit. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono Christ welcomes us to his table. Fed by him, we learn to welcome others.

2026-12-31.title: Thursday after the First Sunday after Yaldo · Last day of the year
readings: The priestly service of the gospel
Let it alone for one more year
2026-12-31.alt: The last day of the civil year: a day of thanksgiving and examination of conscience. Tomorrow, 1 January 2027, is the feast of the Naming of our Lord. Season of Yaldo and Denho.
2026-12-31.verse: He replied, ‘Sir, let it alone for one more year, until I dig around it and put manure on it.
theo: On the last day of the year the Church reads one of the most hopeful parables. A man has a fig tree that has borne no fruit for three years. “Cut it down! Why should it be wasting the soil?” But the gardener pleads: “Sir, let it alone for one more year, until I dig around it and put manure on it. If it bears fruit next year, well and good; but if not, you can cut it down.” Christ is that gardener. Every new year is a gift of patience from God, and also a call to bear fruit.

Paul, near the end of Romans, describes his work as “the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.” He boasts only of what Christ has accomplished through him, in word and deed, from Jerusalem to Illyricum. As we close the year, we offer to God what he has done through us, and ask pardon for the fruit we failed to bear.
outline: What fruit did this year bear?
God's patience is our new year.
Give the year back to God.
“Let it alone for one more year.”
live: Examine the year (Luke 13:7)
Before midnight, thank God for three graces and ask pardon for three failures.
Offer the year (Romans 15:16)
Attend a thanksgiving prayer or Qurbono tonight or tomorrow.
2026-12-31.prayer: Lord Jesus, patient gardener, you have given us another year. Thank you for every grace of this year; forgive the fruit we did not bear; dig around our roots and make us fruitful in the year to come. Amen.
altar: At the last Holy Qurbono of the year we give thanks. The Gardener who pleads for us feeds us for the year to come.

Zechariah's silence ends in praise when he obeys.
Every child is a gift with a mission from God.

2026-12-06.question: What do I need to obey so that my tongue may be freed to praise?
2026-12-06.special: Fourth Sunday of Suboro: the Birth of John the Baptist. The Twenty-Five Days Nombu continues.
illus: An illustration

In many Kerala families the grandfather or the parish priest chooses the child's baptismal name, often a saint's name. Zechariah reminds us that the deepest name comes from God, and carries a mission.

family.explain: Baby John was born, and his father Zechariah, who could not speak for many months, wrote “His name is John”. Then he could speak again, and he praised God!
family.intention: We thank God for every child in our family, and pray for each one by name.
family.ask: Ask: “What does my name mean? Which saint am I named after?”

catechism: The Christian name given at Baptism.
kidsaint: A bishop in Myra (in today's Turkey) in the fourth century, loved for his secret kindness to the poor and to children. Lesson: give in secret, as St Nicholas did, and God sees.
term: Luke 1:68–79, named after its first word in Latin, “Blessed”. The Church prays it every morning in many traditions as a song of praise for the coming of Christ, “the dawn from on high”.
termMore: The Syro-Malankara lectionary follows the order of Luke's Gospel through Suboro: the message to Zechariah, the Annunciation, the Visitation, the birth of John, the message to Joseph, and then the Nativity.

pm.open: Lord God, you gave Zechariah and Elizabeth a son whose name means God is gracious. As we gather on this Sunday of the Birth of John the Baptist, loosen our tongues to praise you. Amen.
share: Zechariah sang: blessed be the Lord God of Israel (Luke 1:68). For what do I bless God this week?
The child grew and became strong in spirit (Luke 1:80). How do we help children grow in faith?
John prepared the way of the Lord. How can I prepare his way at home?
pm.resp: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel.
interc: For the Church, that like John she may point to Christ.
For children, that they may grow strong in spirit.
For parents, that they may receive their children as gifts of God.
For couples who long for a child.
For our parish, that this fast may bear fruit.
pm.close: Lord God, you prepared the way for your Son through John the Baptist. Make us forerunners of Christ in our homes and workplaces. Amen.

quick: Joseph the righteous man is merciful.
God speaks to Joseph in a dream; he listens.
Joseph obeys at once and gives Jesus a home and a name.
2026-12-13.action: Refuse one piece of gossip this week and speak well of that person.
2026-12-13.question: Do I give God enough silence to speak to me?
2026-12-13.special: Fifth Sunday of Suboro: the Apparition of the Angel to St Joseph.
illus: An illustration
A father in the Gulf works twelve hours a day and calls home every night to pray with his children over the phone. No one writes about him, but his family stands because of him. That is Joseph's way.

family.explain: An angel told Joseph in a dream to take care of Mary and her baby. Joseph woke up and did what God said straight away. He became the father who took care of Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for our father and grandfathers, and for all fathers who work far from home.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we thank our father this week?”

catechism: The virginal conception announced to Joseph.
kidsaint: A young Christian of Syracuse in Sicily who gave her riches to the poor and died as a martyr around the year 304. Her name means “light”. Lesson: be a light by your goodness.
term: Matthew calls Joseph “righteous” or “just”, in Hebrew tsaddiq: one whose whole life is in harmony with God's will. In Joseph, justice and mercy meet.
termMore: The Syriac Fathers honour Joseph as the guardian of the Mystery; St Ephrem's Nativity hymns imagine him caring for the Child and marvelling at him.

pm.open: Lord God, you spoke to Joseph in a dream and he obeyed. As we gather on this Sunday of the Apparition of the Angel to St Joseph, give us his faith and courage. Amen.
share: Joseph planned one thing, but God asked another (Matthew 1:19–20). When have I had to change my plans for God?
Joseph did as the angel commanded (Matthew 1:24). What is God asking me to do?
How can fathers in our parish imitate St Joseph?
pm.resp: St Joseph, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that like Joseph she may protect Christ.
For fathers, that they may be just, gentle and brave.
For those facing difficult decisions, that they may hear God's voice.
For families preparing for Yaldo.
For those who are misunderstood, like Mary and Joseph.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you were welcomed and protected by St Joseph. Through his prayers, make our homes places where you are welcomed and loved. Amen.
