2026-12-20.special: Sixth Sunday of Suboro, the Sunday before Yaldo (Christmas, Friday 25 December).
illus: An illustration

At a Kerala family reunion the eldest member reads out the names of the ancestors who brought the faith to the family. The young people discover that their faith has a history. The genealogy of Jesus does the same for the whole Church.

family.explain: Joseph and Mary had to travel a long way to Bethlehem, because the emperor wanted to count everyone. God used that journey so that Jesus would be born in Bethlehem, the town of King David.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and great-grandparents who passed on the faith to us.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught our family to pray? Let us thank God for them.”

catechism: The angel announces the birth of the Messiah in the city of David.
The Holy Scripture in the life of the Church.
kidsaint: A great scholar who lived in Bethlehem and spent his life translating the Bible so that everyone could read it. He said that not knowing the Scriptures means not knowing Christ. Lesson: read a little of the Bible every day.
term: Syriac for “birth”: the feast of the Nativity of our Lord, 25 December. The season of Yaldo–Denho follows, until the Baptism of the Lord (Denho, 6 January).
termMore: Matthew traces Jesus' line from Abraham through David; Luke traces it back to Adam. Both show that Jesus is the Son of David and the Saviour of all humanity.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, son of David, son of Abraham, you entered our human family through many generations. As we gather on the Sunday before Yaldo, bless our families and our ancestors. Amen.
share: Jesus' genealogy includes saints and sinners (Matthew 1:1–17). What does this tell me about God's love for my family?
Who handed on the faith to me?
How will I prepare my heart in the last days before Yaldo?
pm.resp: Son of David, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may welcome Christ with faith at Yaldo.
For our ancestors who handed on the faith.
For families wounded by sin, that Christ may heal them.
For those travelling home for Yaldo.
For our parish, as we complete the Yaldo fast.
pm.close: Lord God, your promises were fulfilled through many generations. Bless our families, heal our history, and make us ready to welcome your Son. Amen.

2026-12-25.action: Invite someone who is alone to share your Christmas meal.
2026-12-25.question: What gift will I bring to the Child this Christmas?
2026-12-25.special: Yaldo, the Nativity of our Lord: a day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people.
illus: An illustration

On Christmas night every Kerala home hangs a star at the door. A small paper star says to every passer-by: here a family is waiting for Christ. The Magi followed a star to a house where they found the Child; may our stars lead others to him.

family.read: Read together at the crib: Luke 2:1–14.
family.explain: Jesus, God's Son, was born as a little baby in Bethlehem. Angels sang, shepherds came, and later wise men brought gifts. God loves us so much that he came to be with us.
family.intention: We pray for families who are sad or alone this Christmas, and for peace in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift can each of us give Jesus this year?”

kidsaint: Learned men from the East who followed a star a long way to find the newborn King. When they found Jesus with Mary, they knelt down and gave him their best gifts. Lesson: look for Jesus, and give him your best.
term: In the Malankara tradition the night service of Yaldo includes a fire, lit with frankincense and often with the palm leaves kept from Hosanna Sunday, while the Gloria of the angels is sung. It proclaims Christ, the Light of the world, born in the night.
termMore: The second season of the Syro-Malankara year: from the Nativity (Yaldo) through the Baptism of the Lord (Denho, 6 January), celebrating God's manifestation in Christ.

pm.open: Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth. Lord Jesus, born for us at Yaldo, we gather with joy around you. Amen.
share: The light shines in the darkness (John 1:5). Where has the light of Christ shone in my life this year?
Micah says the ruler will come from little Bethlehem (Micah 5:2). How does God use small things in my life?
How will I share the joy of Yaldo with someone who is alone?
pm.resp: Glory to God in the highest.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the joy of the Nativity.
For peace in the world, especially in the Holy Land.
For families, that the Child of Bethlehem may dwell in their homes.
For the poor, the homeless and refugees.
For the sick, the lonely and the grieving on this day.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, born of the Virgin Mary, Mother of God, fill our hearts with the joy of Yaldo and make us messengers of your peace. Amen.

2026-12-27.action: Set a fixed time for family prayer every day this week.
2026-12-27.question: Is my home a little Nazareth?
2026-12-27.special: First Sunday after Yaldo. Commemoration of the Infants killed by Herod.
illus: An illustration

A Kerala father once lost his small son at a crowded church festival. For an hour he ran from stall to stall. When he found the boy sitting calmly near the altar, he did not know whether to scold him or hold him. Mary and Joseph knew that feeling.

family.explain: When Jesus was twelve, he stayed behind in the Temple, and his parents searched for him for three days. Jesus said the Temple was his Father's house. Then he went home with them and obeyed them.
family.intention: We pray for our family, that we may love, obey and help one another like the Holy Family.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us make our home more like Nazareth this week?”

catechism: The Christian family, a communion of persons.
kidsaint: Jesus, Mary and Joseph lived in a small house. Joseph worked as a carpenter, Mary cared for the home, and Jesus helped and obeyed them. They prayed together and went to the Temple. Lesson: your family can be holy too.
term: The small village in Galilee where Jesus grew up and lived about thirty years. Christians were first nicknamed “Nazarenes” (Acts 24:5); in Kerala the old name “Nasrani” for St Thomas Christians comes from the same word.
termMore: The children of Bethlehem killed by Herod (Matthew 2:16–18). The Church honours them as the first martyrs for Christ, who died not speaking but in his place.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you lived in Nazareth with Mary and Joseph after the return from Egypt. As we gather on the First Sunday after Yaldo, bless our families. Amen.
share: The Holy Family settled in Nazareth after exile (Matthew 2:19–23). What journeys has my family made?
Peter says: clothe yourselves with humility (1 Peter 5:5). Where is humility needed in my home?
What would make our home more like Nazareth?
pm.resp: Jesus, Mary and Joseph, bless our family.
interc: For all families, that they may imitate the Holy Family.
For migrant and refugee families.
For families separated by work abroad.
For broken families, that they may be healed.
For our parish family.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave your Son a home in Nazareth. Bless our families with faith, humility and love, and keep us united in you. Amen.

Put on the armour of light.

pm.open: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal Word and light of the world, as we begin the fast before Yaldo, wake us from sleep and clothe us with your light. Amen.
share: Paul says love is the fulfilling of the law (Romans 13:10). How can my fast become an act of love?
The night is far gone, the day is near (Romans 13:12). In what area of my life am I still asleep?
What will I fast from until Yaldo?
pm.resp: Lord, wake us and clothe us with your light.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep the Yaldo fast with faith and love.
For our families, that the fast may bring more prayer and peace into our homes.
For those enslaved by alcohol, drugs or screens, that they may be freed.
For the poor, that our fasting may become food for them.
For our prayer group, that we may welcome the light of Christ.
pm.close: Lord God, your eternal Word comes as light into our darkness. Bless our fast, purify our hearts and make us ready to welcome your Son at Yaldo. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in Mavelikara has kept the twenty-five days' fast for sixty years. Every evening of the fast she puts aside a handful of rice for the poor. Her grandchildren now do the same. She says: “The fast is not about what we leave, but about whom we love.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the truth. As we gather, make our words honest and our feet beautiful with the good news. Amen.
share: Paul asks: how will they hear without someone to proclaim? (Romans 10:14). Who first told me about Jesus?
Jesus says: let your yes be yes (Matthew 5:37). Where am I not fully honest?
To whom can I bring good news this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us messengers of your truth.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the good news with joy.
For catechists and Sunday school teachers.
For those who have never heard of Christ, that someone may bring them the good news.
For those who live by lies and deceit, that they may turn to the truth.
For our families, that our words may be trustworthy.
pm.close: Lord God, how beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news. Make us honest in all our words and faithful messengers of your Son. Amen.

illus: An illustration
A shopkeeper in Thiruvalla was known in the whole market for one thing: “If he says yes, it is yes.” Many customers who were not Christians said they first respected the Church because of him.

St Francis Xavier preached along the coasts of South India.
2026-12-03.action: Pray for one missionary from your parish or eparchy.
2026-12-03.question: What comfort would I give up for the Gospel?

family.explain: Jesus told his friends to go everywhere and tell everyone the good news. St Francis Xavier came to India to tell people about Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries, especially from our Church.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family share Jesus with someone this week?”

pm.open: Lord of the harvest, you sent your apostles into all the world and brought St Francis Xavier to our shores. Fill us with his zeal as we gather. Amen.
share: Paul says: I have become all things to all people (1 Corinthians 9:22). How can I adapt myself to reach others with love?
Jesus says: go into all the world (Mark 16:15). Where is my ‘world’?
What missionary do I know, and how can I support them?
pm.resp: Lord, send us to proclaim your love.
interc: For missionaries throughout the world, especially from our Church.
For the mission of the Syro-Malankara Church in North India and abroad.
For the people of India's coasts, evangelised by St Francis Xavier.
For vocations to the missionary life.
For our families, that they may be witnesses of Christ.
pm.close: Lord God, through St Francis Xavier you brought the Gospel to our land. Through his prayers, give us zeal and joy to share the good news. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A young Malankara Catholic engineer in Pune began inviting his colleagues from other states for Sunday lunch at his small flat. Over food they asked about his faith. Two years later one of them asked to be baptised.

quick: Anger is the root of murder.
Be reconciled before you offer your gift.
Faith comes from hearing the word of Christ.
2026-12-04.action: Take one step today toward reconciliation.
2026-12-04.question: Whom must I be reconciled with before Christmas?

family.explain: Jesus says if we are angry with someone, we should make peace before we come to God's altar.
family.intention: We pray for peace in our family and with our neighbours.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we need to make peace with?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us to be reconciled before we bring our gifts. As we gather, heal our anger and make us peacemakers. Amen.
share: Jesus warns against anger and insults (Matthew 5:22). When do I lose my temper?
Is there someone who has something against me?
What does the kiss of peace at the Holy Qurbono mean to me?
pm.resp: Lord, make us instruments of your peace.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a community of reconciliation.
For families divided by anger and quarrels.
For theologians and teachers of the faith, through the prayers of St John of Damascus.
For those who have not sought God, that he may find them.
For our group, that we may be at peace with one another.
pm.close: Lord God, through St John of Damascus you taught your Church to honour the image of your Son. Heal our anger and make us reconciled, so that our offering may please you. Amen.

illus: An illustration

Two neighbours in Kottarakkara had fought over a boundary wall for years. One Friday, after the kiss of peace at the Qurbono, one of them walked over to the other's house. They are now godparents to each other's grandchildren.

quick: Train yourself in godliness.
Our hope is in the living God.
Never has anyone spoken like Jesus.
2026-12-05.action: Add five minutes of silent prayer each day of the fast.
2026-12-05.question: Have I given Jesus a fair hearing?

family.explain: Paul says we should train our souls like athletes train their bodies. Prayer and good habits make us strong in God.
family.intention: We pray for monks, nuns and all who live a life of prayer.
family.ask: Ask: “What good habit can we practise together during this fast?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, never has anyone spoken like you. As we gather, train us in godliness and give us courage to stand up for you. Amen.
share: Paul says godliness is valuable in every way (1 Timothy 4:8). What spiritual exercise do I need most?
The guards said: never has anyone spoken like this (John 7:46). Which words of Jesus have touched me most?
Like Nicodemus, where can I take a small step of courage for Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, train us in your ways.
interc: For monks and nuns, through the prayers of Mar Saba.
For teachers of the faith, through the prayers of St Clement of Alexandria.
For those divided about Jesus, that they may come to know him.
For the timid, that they may find courage to witness.
For our group, that we may grow in godliness.
pm.close: Lord God, Mar Saba and St Clement trained themselves in godliness. Help us to keep this fast as training of the soul, and to grow in faith step by step. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A college student in Thiruvananthapuram decided during the Yaldo fast to wake up fifteen minutes early each day to read the Gospel. By the end of the fast she had read all of Luke. She said: “It was the first time I really heard Jesus speak.”

quick: Paul knows the one he has trusted.
Guard the treasure of faith with the Spirit's help.
Jesus has conquered the world.
2026-12-07.action: Name one fear and hand it to Jesus.
2026-12-07.question: Am I ashamed of the Gospel anywhere?

family.explain: Jesus says: in the world you will have troubles, but be brave, I have won. Jesus is always with us.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard for us to show we are Christians?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have conquered the world. As we gather, take away our shame and fear, and give us courage to witness. Amen.
share: Paul says: do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord (2 Timothy 1:8). When am I ashamed of my faith?
Paul says: I know the one in whom I have put my trust (2 Timothy 1:12). How deep is my trust in Jesus?
Jesus says: take courage (John 16:33). What trouble do I need courage for?
pm.resp: Take courage; Christ has conquered the world.
interc: For persecuted Christians in India and the world.
For young people mocked for their faith.
For Christians working abroad, that they may be faithful witnesses.
For those who feel alone, that they may know the Father is with them.
For our group, that we may not be ashamed of the Gospel.
pm.close: Lord God, you called us with a holy calling. Give us courage and trust, so that we may never be ashamed of your Son, who has conquered the world. Amen.

illus: An illustration
A Malankara Catholic student in a hostel in Hyderabad was mocked for praying before meals. She kept doing it quietly. By the end of the year, three of her friends were praying with her.

quick: Mary was preserved from original sin from her conception.
This grace came from the merits of her Son.
She answers with praise: the Mighty One has done great things.
2026-12-08.question: What great things has God done for me?

family.explain: God kept Mary free from sin from the very beginning, so that she could be Jesus' mother. Mary sang a song of praise to God.
family.intention: We pray for mothers and for purity of heart in our family.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be more like Mary this week?”

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God, preserved from every stain of sin, pray with us as we gather, that our hearts may become a pure dwelling for your Son. Amen.
share: Mary calls God my Saviour (Luke 1:47). How has God saved me?
What sin keeps my heart from being a pure dwelling for Jesus?
How will I prepare for confession before Yaldo?
pm.resp: Holy Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that she may be holy and without blemish.
For young people, that they may grow in purity of heart.
For mothers, that Mary may guide and protect them.
For sinners, that they may return to God through confession.
For our families, that we may honour Mary by imitating her.
pm.close: Lord God, you preserved the Virgin Mary from every stain of sin. Through her prayers, cleanse our hearts and make them a home for your Son. Amen.

illus: An illustration

An elderly priest in Thiruvalla was asked what the Immaculate Conception meant to him. He said: “It means God can make something perfectly beautiful in this world. And if he did it in Mary, he can begin to do it in me.”

quick: God has spoken finally in his Son.
John asked: are you the one?
Jesus answers with works of mercy.
2026-12-09.action: Write down three things God has done for you this year.
2026-12-09.question: What question do I want to bring to Jesus?

family.explain: God spoke through many prophets, but his best and final word is Jesus. Jesus shows us exactly what God is like.
family.intention: We pray for the sick and the poor.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do this week to show that Jesus has come?”

pm.open: Lord God, in these last days you have spoken to us by your Son. As we gather, open our ears to his word and our hands to his works. Amen.
share: God has spoken by a Son (Hebrews 1:2). How much time do I give to listening to Jesus in the Gospel?
Jesus points to signs of mercy (Luke 7:22). What sign of mercy can I do this week?
What question would I like to ask Jesus, as John did?
pm.resp: Speak, Lord, your servants are listening.
interc: For the Church, that she may listen to the Son and do his works.
For the sick and disabled, that they may experience Christ's mercy.
For prisoners, like John, that they may find hope.
For those who doubt, that they may see the signs of Christ.
For our group, that we may grow in love for the Word.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son is the reflection of your glory. Help us to listen to him and to do his works of mercy, as we prepare for his birth at Yaldo. Amen.

illus: An illustration
A parish youth group in Adoor visited a home for the disabled every Sunday of the Yaldo fast. One resident said: “When you come, I know that Jesus has really come.”

quick: Do not fear those who kill only the body.
You are worth more than many sparrows.
Acknowledge Christ and he will acknowledge you.
2026-12-10.action: Say grace openly at your next meal with others.
2026-12-10.question: Where do I hide my faith?

family.explain: God knows every little bird and even counts the hairs on our heads. We do not need to be afraid, because God loves us so much.
family.intention: We pray for family members who are far away or in danger.
family.ask: Ask: “What are we afraid of, and how can we trust God with it?”

pm.open: Heavenly Father, not a sparrow falls without you. As we gather, take away our fears and teach us to love more and more. Amen.
share: Jesus says: do not be afraid (Matthew 10:31). What fear do I bring to the Father today?
Paul says: love more and more (1 Thessalonians 4:10). Whom can I love more this week?
Where do I need courage to acknowledge Jesus before others?
pm.resp: Father, we trust in your care.
interc: For the Church, that she may confess Christ without fear.
For family members abroad or in danger, that the Father may protect them.
For those who live in fear and anxiety.
For workers, that they may find dignity in their work.
For our group, that we may grow in love.
pm.close: Heavenly Father, you count every hair of our heads. Free us from fear, help us to love more and more, and give us courage to confess your Son. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A mother in Pathanamthitta, worried about her son working in a dangerous job abroad, wrote Matthew 10:31 on a card and put it on her prayer table. She says: “Every morning I read it and give him to the Father who counts his hairs.”

quick: Sunday and care for the poor belong together.
God desires mercy, not sacrifice.
Jesus is Lord of the sabbath.
2026-12-11.action: Give the money saved by fasting to the poor.
2026-12-11.question: Is my fasting turning into mercy?

family.explain: Jesus says God wants mercy more than rules. Being kind to people is more important than being strict.
family.intention: We pray for poor families this Yaldo.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we save during this fast to give to someone in need?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you desire mercy and not sacrifice. As we gather, make our fasting merciful and our giving generous. Amen.
share: Paul asks for regular giving (1 Corinthians 16:2). Is my giving planned and generous?
Jesus says: I desire mercy (Matthew 12:7). Does my faith make me more merciful?
To whom will I give what I save during this fast?
pm.resp: Lord, make us merciful.
interc: For the Church, that she may be known for her mercy.
For the poor and hungry, especially at Yaldo.
For those who use religion to judge others, that they may learn mercy.
For our parish charities.
For our group, that our fast may bear the fruit of mercy.
pm.close: Lord God, you desire mercy more than sacrifice. Let our fast become generosity, and our worship lead us to love our neighbour. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A family in Kollam keeps a box on their dining table during the Yaldo fast. Every time they skip meat or a treat, they put the money saved inside. On Yaldo morning they give it to a family who cannot afford a festive meal.

quick: Rejoice, pray, give thanks: God's will for us.
Cut off whatever leads into sin.
Have salt in yourselves and be at peace.
2026-12-12.action: Remove one thing that regularly leads you into sin.
2026-12-12.question: Have I lost my saltiness?

family.explain: Paul says: be joyful always, pray always, and say thank you to God for everything.
family.intention: We thank God for our family.
family.ask: Ask: “What are we thankful for today?”

pm.open: Holy Spirit, we will not quench your fire. As we gather, teach us to rejoice always, pray without ceasing and give thanks in all things. Amen.
share: Paul says: give thanks in all circumstances (1 Thessalonians 5:18). What hard circumstance can I thank God in?
Jesus speaks of stumbling blocks (Mark 9:42). What stumbling block do I need to remove?
How can I be salt in my family and workplace?
pm.resp: Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all things.
interc: For the Church, that she may be salt of the earth.
For children, that no one may cause them to stumble.
For the faint-hearted and the weak, that they may be encouraged.
For priests and all who labour in the Church.
For our group, that we may be at peace with one another.
pm.close: Lord God, it is your will that we rejoice, pray and give thanks. Fill us with your Spirit, remove what makes us stumble, and make us salt for the world. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A teacher in Kottayam began a simple habit with her class: at the end of each day, every student wrote one thing they were thankful for. By the end of the year, she said, the whole atmosphere of the class had changed.

quick: Melchizedek, priest of bread and wine, points to Christ.
Discipleship means carrying the cross.
Count the cost and finish the work.
2026-12-14.action: Bear one difficulty today without complaining.
2026-12-14.question: What cross am I avoiding?

family.explain: Jesus wants to be first in our lives, even before family and friends. Following Jesus is worth everything.
family.intention: We pray for those who give up much to follow Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we put Jesus first in our family?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, eternal High Priest, you call us to follow you with all our heart. As we gather, help us to count the cost and choose you. Amen.
share: Jesus says whoever does not carry the cross cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:27). What cross am I avoiding?
What do I put before Jesus?
How has God blessed me when I put him first?
pm.resp: Lord, you are first in our lives.
interc: For priests, that they may be faithful to Christ the eternal High Priest.
For those who leave everything to follow Christ.
For contemplatives, through the prayers of St John of the Cross.
For those who are afraid of the cost of discipleship.
For our families, that Jesus may be first in our homes.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son is priest for ever. Give us courage to put him first, to carry our cross and to follow him with all our hearts. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A young doctor from Kerala was offered a well-paid post in the US, but felt called to work in a mission hospital in Jharkhand. Her parents were upset. She said: “I counted the cost. Jesus is worth it.” Years later her parents visit her hospital every Christmas.

quick: Paul preached only Christ crucified.
Faith rests on God's power, not human wisdom.
Jesus warns us so that we will not stumble.
2026-12-15.action: Pray five minutes before a crucifix today.
2026-12-15.question: Is my faith built on cleverness or on Christ?

family.explain: Paul was a clever man, but he told people only about Jesus who died on the cross for us. God's power is greater than human cleverness.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are persecuted.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show God's love even to people who are unkind to us?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, crucified and risen, you are the power and wisdom of God. As we gather, strengthen us in weakness and give us courage in trials. Amen.
share: Paul decided to know nothing but Christ crucified (1 Corinthians 2:2). What is at the centre of my faith?
Jesus warned of persecution (John 16:2). How do I respond when I am treated unfairly for my faith?
Where do I rely on my cleverness instead of God's power?
pm.resp: Lord, your power is made perfect in weakness.
interc: For persecuted Christians in India and the world.
For those who persecute in God's name, that they may know the true God.
For preachers, that they may proclaim Christ crucified.
For those who feel weak and afraid.
For our group, that our faith may rest on the power of God.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son was crucified in weakness and raised in power. Strengthen persecuted Christians, convert their persecutors, and let our faith rest on you alone. Amen.

illus: An illustration

In 1999 the missionary Graham Staines and his two young sons were burnt to death in Odisha. His widow, Gladys Staines, publicly forgave the killers and continued serving leprosy patients in India (H). Her forgiveness spoke of Christ crucified more powerfully than any argument.

quick: Jesus asks: who do you say that I am?
Peter answers: the Messiah of God.
Grace is enough; power is perfected in weakness.
2026-12-16.action: Write in one sentence who Jesus is for you.
2026-12-16.question: What is my answer to Jesus' question?

family.explain: Jesus asked his friends: who do you say I am? Peter said: you are the Messiah, God's chosen one.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sick or suffering.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is Jesus for each of us?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Messiah of God, you ask us: who do you say that I am? As we gather, let us answer you with faith, and receive your grace in our weakness. Amen.
share: Jesus asks: who do you say that I am? (Luke 9:20). What is my personal answer?
Paul heard: my grace is sufficient for you (2 Corinthians 12:9). What thorn do I carry?
How has God's power worked in my weakness?
pm.resp: Your grace is sufficient for us, Lord.
interc: For the Church, that she may confess Christ with faith.
For the chronically ill and those in pain.
For those whose prayers seem unanswered, that they may find sufficient grace.
For those who do not know who Jesus is.
For our group, that we may know Jesus through prayer.
pm.close: Lord God, your power is made perfect in weakness. Help us to confess your Son as the Messiah, and to carry our thorns with his grace. Amen.

illus: An illustration
A young man in Thiruvananthapuram with a chronic illness said: “For years I asked God to heal me. Now I ask him to use me. Since then, my illness has brought me closer to many people who suffer.”

quick: Be wise in good, innocent in evil.
False prophets are known by their fruits.
The God of peace will crush Satan.
2026-12-17.action: Check religious content for faithfulness before sharing it.
2026-12-17.question: What fruit does my life bear?

family.explain: Jesus says we know a tree by its fruit. Good people show their goodness by what they do.
family.intention: We pray that our family may bear good fruit.
family.ask: Ask: “What good fruit did each of us bear this week?”

pm.open: God of peace, you will crush evil under our feet. As we gather, keep us faithful to the teaching we have received and make us bear good fruit. Amen.
share: Paul warns against those who cause divisions (Romans 16:17). Am I a source of unity or division?
Jesus says: you will know them by their fruits (Matthew 7:16). What fruit does my faith bear?
Which voices do I listen to about God, and are they trustworthy?
pm.resp: Lord, make us good trees bearing good fruit.
interc: For the Church, that she may remain united in the true faith.
For those deceived by false teachers, that they may find the truth.
For the bishops of our Church, that they may guard the flock.
For those who cause division, that they may be converted.
For our families, that they may bear good fruit.
pm.close: Lord God, you promised to crush the serpent's head. Keep us in the true faith, protect us from deception, and make our lives fruitful in love. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A family in Kottayam was drawn into a group that promised miracles in exchange for large donations. The fruits were debt and quarrels. Their parish priest gently helped them return. The father said: “I learnt to look at the fruits, not the noise.”

quick: Jesus prepares a place for us in the Father's house.
He is the way, the truth and the life.
The ancient cross of Mylapore witnesses to early Christianity in India.
2026-12-18.action: Hand over one worry to Jesus today.
2026-12-18.question: Do I let Jesus be my way?

family.explain: Jesus said he is going to prepare a place for us in his Father's house. Jesus is the way to God.
family.intention: We pray for those who are dying and for those who mourn.
family.ask: Ask: “What does it mean that Jesus is the way?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, the way, the truth and the life, as we gather, calm our troubled hearts and show us the boundless riches of your love. Amen.
share: Jesus says: do not let your hearts be troubled (John 14:1). What troubles my heart?
Thomas asked: how can we know the way? (John 14:5). What honest question do I bring to Jesus?
What riches of Christ have I received through my Church?
pm.resp: Lord, you are the way, the truth and the life.
interc: For the Syro-Malankara Church, that she may treasure and share her heritage.
For those whose hearts are troubled.
For the dying, that they may find the way to the Father's house.
For those who search for truth.
For our group, that we may walk with Christ.
pm.close: Lord God, through the Church your manifold wisdom is made known. Keep us on the way of your Son, and bring us to the dwelling he has prepared for us. Amen.

illus: An illustration
An old man in Ranni, nearing death, asked his grandson to read John 14 every evening. After the reading he would say: “There is a room ready for me.” He died peacefully on the morning of Yaldo.

quick: We are built into a dwelling place for God.
Christ brings peace to the far and the near.
The signs of the kingdom: the blind see, the poor hear good news.
2026-12-19.action: Prepare your home's prayer corner for Yaldo.
2026-12-19.question: Is my heart ready to be God's dwelling?

family.explain: Jesus breaks down walls between people. In God's family no one is a stranger.
family.intention: We pray for unity among Christians and peace among all people.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone different from us whom we can welcome?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are our peace; you break down the dividing walls. As we gather, make us one family in you. Amen.
share: Paul says: you are no longer strangers (Ephesians 2:19). Whom do I treat as a stranger?
Jesus says: blessed is anyone who takes no offence at me (Matthew 11:6). Do I accept Jesus as he is?
What wall can I help break down this Yaldo?
pm.resp: Christ is our peace.
interc: For the unity of all Christians.
For peace between communities in our country.
For those divided by caste, language or politics.
For the poor, that they may hear good news.
For our group, that we may welcome strangers.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son broke down the walls that divide us. Make us one household in him, built on the apostles and prophets, with Christ as the cornerstone. Amen.

illus: An illustration

In a housing colony in Kochi, families of different Churches and religions had never mixed. One Yaldo a Malankara Catholic family invited all their neighbours for a Christmas meal. It became an annual tradition, and the colony now calls it “our feast”.

quick: Faith is a gift we owe to others.
We are mutually encouraged by each other's faith.
The Word through whom all was made becomes a child.
2026-12-21.action: Send a Christmas message that speaks of Jesus.
2026-12-21.question: Whose faith can I encourage this Christmas?

family.explain: Jesus was with God before the world began. He made everything, and he is the light no darkness can put out.
family.intention: We pray for those who live far from home and need encouragement.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we encourage in their faith this week?”

pm.open: Eternal Word of the Father, light of all people, as we gather, let us be encouraged by one another's faith and share your light. Amen.
share: Paul says we are mutually encouraged by each other's faith (Romans 1:12). Whose faith encourages me?
Paul says: I am a debtor (Romans 1:14). To whom do I owe the Gospel?
How does it change my view of Yaldo to know the Child is the eternal Word?
pm.resp: Christ our light, shine upon us.
interc: For the Church, that her faith may be proclaimed throughout the world.
For young people studying and working far from home.
For those whose faith is weak, that they may be encouraged.
For all who live in darkness, that the light may reach them.
For our group, that we may encourage one another.
pm.close: Lord God, your Word was in the beginning with you. Fill us with his life and light, and make us encourage one another in faith as we await his birth. Amen.

illus: An illustration

Every Yaldo week, an elderly couple in Kayamkulam writes short letters of encouragement to the young people of their parish who are studying or working away from home. Many of those young people keep the letters for years.

quick: John came to bear witness to the light.
Christ is the true light for everyone.
Faith begins with being known by God.
2026-12-22.action: Put a light in your window as a sign of Christ.
2026-12-22.question: To whom can I point the light?

family.explain: John the Baptist was not the light, but he pointed to Jesus, the true light.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always point others to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we point people to Jesus, like John?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true light that enlightens everyone, as we gather in these last days of the fast, turn our eyes from ourselves to you. Amen.
share: Paul says we are known by God (Galatians 4:9). What does it mean to me that God knows me?
Has my fast been about earning God's favour or opening my heart?
Like John, how can I witness to the light?
pm.resp: Christ, true light, enlighten us.
interc: For the Church, that she may point always to Christ.
For those who rely on observances without love.
For those who do not yet know God, that they may know they are known by him.
For witnesses of the faith in our time.
For our group, as we complete the Yaldo fast.
pm.close: Lord God, you knew us before we knew you. Free us from earning your love, and let the true light of your Son shine in our hearts at Yaldo. Amen.

illus: An illustration
A boy once asked his grandmother why she kept every fast so carefully. She said: “Not to make God love me, mone. He already does. I fast so that I can love him more.”

quick: The world did not know him; his own did not accept him.
To all who receive him he gives power to become God's children.
All treasures of wisdom are hidden in Christ.
2026-12-23.action: Make room in your Christmas for someone who is alone.
2026-12-23.question: Have I truly received him?

family.explain: Some people did not welcome Jesus. But those who welcome him become God's children.
family.intention: We pray that our family may welcome Jesus at Yaldo.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make room for Jesus in our home this Yaldo?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, in you are hidden all the treasures of wisdom. As we gather two days before Yaldo, help us to receive you and become children of God. Amen.
share: In Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom (Colossians 2:3). How well do I know Christ?
His own did not accept him (John 1:11). Where is there no room for him in my life?
How will I receive him at Yaldo?
pm.resp: Lord, we receive you with joy.
interc: For the Church, that she may receive Christ with faith and love.
For those who do not know Christ, that they may receive him.
For families preparing for Yaldo, that they may make room for Jesus.
For the homeless, who share the lot of the Holy Family.
For our group, that we may become true children of God.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son came to his own. Open our hearts to receive him, and make us your children through faith in his name. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A young couple in Adoor, expecting their first child, decided to give their Yaldo shopping budget to a family whose house had been damaged by rain. The wife said: “We wanted Jesus to find room in our home this year.”

quick: The Word became flesh and lived among us.
From his fullness we receive grace upon grace.
Christ is the true Image of God, not an idol.
2026-12-24.action: Come to the festal Qurbono of Yaldo with a prepared heart.
2026-12-24.question: Is my heart ready to receive him tomorrow?

family.explain: The Word became a human being and lived among us. Jesus shows us exactly what God is like.
family.intention: We pray for all families gathering tonight, and for those who are alone.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift will each of us give to Jesus tonight?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Word made flesh, full of grace and truth, on this Eve of Yaldo we wait for you with joy. Enlighten our hearts. Amen.
share: Paul says humanity exchanged God's glory for images (Romans 1:23). What false images take God's place in my life?

What grace upon grace have I received this year?
pm.resp: Come, Lord Jesus, come.

For families gathering for Yaldo, that they may be united in love.
For those alone, sick or grieving tonight.
For the poor and homeless, who share the poverty of Bethlehem.
For peace in the Holy Land and throughout the world.
pm.close: Lord God, your only Son has made you known. Fill us tonight with grace upon grace, and let your Word dwell in our hearts and homes. Amen.

pm.resp: Holy Mother of God, pray for us.

For our families, that we may honour Mary.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of David and Lord of David, as we gather, give us David's faith and his humble heart that returns to you. Amen.
share: Hebrews speaks of those of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:38). Who are such people in my life?
David repented with all his heart. What do I need to repent of?
Jesus is David's son and David's Lord (Matthew 22:42–45). Who is Jesus for me?
pm.resp: Have mercy on us, O God, in your steadfast love.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a home for repentant sinners.
For those who suffer for their faith.
For prisoners, that they may find God's mercy.
For leaders, that like David at his best they may administer justice.
For our group, that we may grow in faith and humility.
pm.close: Lord God, you fulfilled your promise to David in your Son. Give us faith in trials and a contrite heart when we fall, and bring us to your kingdom. Amen.

A man in prison in Thiruvananthapuram began reading the Psalms. Psalm 51 broke his heart. He wrote to his family asking forgiveness, and later to the family he had wronged. The prison chaplain said: “He found David's way home.”

pm.open: Lord God, your gifts and calling are irrevocable. As we gather, make our hearts close to you, not only our lips. Amen.
share: Paul says God has mercy on all (Romans 11:32). Whom do I find hard to see as receiving God's mercy?
Jesus quotes: their hearts are far from me (Matthew 15:8). Where is my heart far from God?
How can I honour my parents better?
pm.resp: Lord, draw our hearts close to you.
interc: For the Church, that her traditions may always serve love.
For the Jewish people, beloved of God.
For elderly parents, that their children may care for them.
For those whose religion is only on their lips.
For our group, that we may honour God with our hearts.
pm.close: Lord God, your mercy is for all. Keep our traditions alive with love, and make our hearts close to you and to our neighbours. Amen.

pm.open: God of hope, fill us with all joy and peace in believing. As we gather near the end of the year, teach us to welcome one another as Christ welcomed us. Amen.
share: Paul says: welcome one another as Christ welcomed you (Romans 15:7). Whom do I find hard to welcome?
Joseph changed plans as God guided him (Matthew 2:22). How has God guided my family this year?
What do I hope for in the new year?
pm.resp: God of hope, fill us with joy and peace.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a welcoming home.
For migrant families and those who have moved for work.
For refugees, who share the road of the Holy Family.
For those without hope, that the Spirit may fill them.
For our group, as we prepare for the new year.
pm.close: Lord God, you guided the Holy Family step by step. Fill us with hope, teach us to welcome one another, and lead us safely into the new year. Amen.

share: Paul speaks of what Christ accomplished through him (Romans 15:18). What has Christ done through me this year?
The gardener asked for one more year (Luke 13:8). What fruit is God waiting for from me?
What is my resolution for the new year?

For pardon for our sins and failures.
For those who died this year.
For peace and holiness in the new year.
For our families and our parish.
pm.close: Lord God, you have given us one more year. Accept our thanks, forgive our sins, and make us bear fruit for your glory in the year to come. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A family in Thiruvalla ends every year by placing three papers before the crib: a thanksgiving, a sorrow and a resolution. They read last year's papers first. The father says: “It shows us how patient God has been with us.”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we celebrate a birthday: the birth of John the Baptist. The neighbours rejoiced with Elizabeth, because God had shown her great mercy. And then came a small argument about the name. The relatives said, “Call him Zechariah, after his father.” Elizabeth said, “No; he is to be called John.”

Zechariah, still unable to speak, asked for a tablet and wrote: “His name is John.” And immediately his mouth was opened, his tongue was freed, and he began to praise God. For nine months his doubt had kept him silent. When he obeyed the word of God, he could speak again, and his first words were praise.

Our readings speak of other children of promise: Moses drawn out of the water, Samuel whom Hannah gave back to the Lord. The psalm says, “Children are a heritage from the Lord.” Dear parents, your children are not your possession; they are God's gift, and each one has a mission. Bless them, pray for them by name, and help them discover what God wants of them.

John's father sang of the coming of “the dawn from on high” to give light to those who sit in darkness. That is what we wait for in this Nombu. Like John, let us prepare the way: with a good Confession, with prayer, with kindness. And let our tongues, like Zechariah's, be freed to bless the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what your name means? John's name means “God is kind”. His father Zechariah could not talk for many months.
When baby John was born, Zechariah wrote on a board: “His name is John.” And suddenly he could talk again! The first thing he did was to praise God.
Tonight, ask your parents why they chose your name. And let's say together: “Thank you, God, for my name!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, this Sunday the Gospel turns from Mary to Joseph. Joseph has made his plans: he is betrothed to Mary, he is preparing a home. Then he discovers that she is with child, and he does not understand.

What does he do? St Matthew says that Joseph, being a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, decided to send her away quietly. Notice: his righteousness is mercy. He does not want to shame her. How different from our world, where people love to expose others on social media and in gossip!

Then God speaks to him in a dream: “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife.” And Joseph, who never speaks a word in the Gospels, simply obeys: he woke up and did as the angel commanded. No delay, no argument. Like young Samuel he could say: “Speak, Lord, your servant is listening.”

Joseph gave Jesus a home, a family name and a father's protection. Dear fathers, your quiet work, your sacrifices, your faithfulness are part of God's plan. And all of us: let us give God some silence each night, so that, like Joseph, we may hear him and obey. Amen.
kids: Children, Joseph was a carpenter who loved Mary. One night an angel came to him in a dream and said: “Don't be afraid! Take care of Mary and her baby Jesus.”
When Joseph woke up, he did exactly what God said, straight away. He became Jesus' father on earth. He kept Jesus safe and taught him to work.
Let's thank God for our fathers. And let's be like Joseph: when Mummy or Daddy asks, do it straight away! Let's say: “Like Joseph, I will listen and obey!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this last Sunday before Yaldo, the Church gives us a list of names: the family of Jacob going down to Egypt, and the genealogy of Jesus. Some of us may wonder why. But these names tell us something beautiful: God did not save the world from a distance. He came through a family, generation after generation.

Isaiah uses a picture every farmer in Kerala knows. A tree is cut down; only a stump remains. Then one day a green shoot appears. “A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse.” When the house of David seemed finished, God was preparing the Saviour. When something in our life seems cut down, God can still make it sprout.

Then St Luke tells us how Mary and Joseph came to Bethlehem. Not by their own plan, but because the emperor ordered a census. A very inconvenient journey for a woman expecting a child! Yet God used it so that his Son would be born in the city of David, as the prophet had promised. God can use even the inconvenient events of our lives.

This week, pray for your family tree: for grandparents and great-grandparents who passed on the faith. Make your Christmas Confession. And on Christmas Eve, gather your family and read the Gospel of the Nativity together. Let us go to Bethlehem, the house of bread, to welcome the Saviour. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know the names of your grandparents? Jesus had grandparents and great-great-grandparents too! The Bible gives a long list of them, all the way back to Abraham and King David.
Mary and Joseph had to walk a long way to Bethlehem. It was hard, but God had a plan: Jesus would be born in the town of King David.
This Christmas, let's thank God for our family. Let's say together: “Thank you, God, for my family!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a happy and blessed Yaldo to all of you! Since Qudos Eetho we have walked through the season of Suboro: the angel in the Temple, the angel in Nazareth, the Visitation, the birth of John, the dream of Joseph. Tonight the waiting is over. “The Word became flesh and lived among us.”

God did not send us only a letter or a messenger. He came himself. The One who made the stars lies in a manger. The One whom heaven cannot contain is held in Mary's arms. That is the wonder of this night: the eternal Son of God is truly one of us, true God and true man.

Isaiah said: “The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.” Many of us bring some darkness to church tonight: a grave visited this year, a son or daughter far away, a debt, an illness, a broken relationship. The Light has come exactly for that darkness. And the darkness has not overcome it.

Our Gospel tells of the Magi, strangers from the East, who followed a star and knelt before the Child with Mary his mother. They offered gold, frankincense and myrrh. What will we offer? Perhaps a reconciliation, a new start at prayer, a gift to someone in need. Come, let us adore him. And in a few moments, at this altar, the same Lord comes to us as the Bread of Life. Glory to God in the highest! Amen.
kids: Children, happy Christmas! Tonight we celebrate Jesus' birthday. God loved us so much that he sent his Son as a tiny baby, born in Bethlehem.
Angels sang, shepherds came running, and wise men followed a bright star to bring him gifts: gold, incense and myrrh.
What gift can you give Jesus? A kind heart, a prayer, sharing your toys! Let's sing with the angels: “Glory to God in the highest!”

intro: Bethlehem means house of bread. The Child born there was laid in a manger, a feeding trough. From the first day, He offered Himself as food.

sub: Bethlehem: Beth-lehem, house of bread.
God chose the town's name with care.
The Bread of Life is born in the House of Bread.
points.apply: At Communion today, remember Bethlehem.

Christmas leads to the Holy Qurbono.

Christmas joy grows when shared.
Feed someone who is hungry this Christmas.

concl: The Child of Bethlehem continues to give Himself as Bread on our altars.
Christmas is fulfilled when we receive Him and share Him.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will receive Communion with the faith of the shepherds and share my bread with someone in need.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a joyful and blessed Christmas to all of you! Tonight let us go in spirit to a small town in Judea. Its name was Bethlehem. In Hebrew, Bethlehem means house of bread. It was there, and nowhere else, that God chose to be born.

The prophet Micah had foretold it: from you, Bethlehem, small among the clans of Judah, shall come forth one who is to rule in Israel (Micah 5:2). God plans with care. The One who would say I am the bread of life (John 6:35) was born in the house of bread.

And where did Mary lay Him? In a manger (Luke 2:7). We have made the crib beautiful with lights and decorations, but a manger was a feeding trough, the place where animals came to eat. The prophet Isaiah had said that the ox knows its owner and the donkey its master's crib, but Israel does not understand (Isaiah 1:3). The Son of God was placed where food is placed. From His first night on earth He was saying: I have come to be your food.

That is why Christmas leads us to the altar. In a few moments, on this altar, the same Christ born in Bethlehem will become present under the appearance of bread. The shepherds knelt at the manger; we kneel before the Holy Qurbono. They saw a child; we see bread. In both cases faith sees God hidden in humility. Receive Him tonight with the faith of the shepherds.

And the shepherds did not keep the good news to themselves. They told everyone what they had heard (Luke 2:17). Bread is meant to be shared. This Christmas, share your bread with someone who is hungry, lonely or forgotten: a meal, a visit, a phone call. Then Christmas will not end tonight. It will continue in every house where Christ, the Bread of Life, is received and shared.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the Incarnation, true God and true man
intro: Christmas is not only a sweet story. It is the heart of our faith: God became man.

sub: The eternal Son took a human nature (John 1:14).
Not a phantom, not a half-god.
For us and for our salvation (Nicene Creed).
points.apply: Bow deeply at the words of the Creed: and became man.

sub: One divine Person, two natures (CCC 464–469).
Councils of Nicaea, Ephesus, Chalcedon.
Mary is truly Mother of God, Theotokos (CCC 495).
points.apply: Call Mary Mother of God with faith in the Hail Mary.

sub: To reconcile us with God (CCC 457).
To show us God's love (CCC 458).
To be our model of holiness and to make us sharers in the divine nature (CCC 459–460).
points.apply: Thank God that He came to make you His child.

concl: The Incarnation is the greatest proof of God's love.
God became man so that we might share His divine life.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will bow at the words of the Creed and thank God for becoming man.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed Christmas to you all! We have heard the familiar story again: the journey, the manger, the shepherds. But behind the story is the most astonishing truth ever proclaimed: God became man. Tonight let us look at this mystery as the Church teaches it.

St John writes: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; and the Word became flesh and lived among us (John 1:1, 14). The Child in the manger is not a good man whom God later adopted, nor a god who only seemed human. He is the eternal Son of God who took to Himself a full human nature, body and soul, in the womb of the Virgin Mary. That is why, in the Creed, at the words and became man, we bow; on Christmas day, we kneel.

The early Church had to defend this truth against many errors. The Councils of Nicaea, Ephesus and Chalcedon taught that Jesus Christ is one divine Person in two natures, divine and human, without confusion and without separation (CCC 464–469). Because the Child is God, the Council of Ephesus proclaimed Mary Theotokos, Mother of God (CCC 495). This is not an exaggeration about Mary; it is a protection of the truth about Jesus.

Why did God become man? The Catechism gives four reasons. To save us by reconciling us with God. So that we might know God's love. To be our model of holiness. And to make us partakers of the divine nature (CCC 457–460; 2 Peter 1:4). The Fathers of the Church summed it up: the Son of God became a son of man so that we might become children of God.

So Christmas is not only for children; it is the foundation of our whole faith. At this Holy Qurbono the same Word made flesh comes to us. Let us receive Him with wonder, and let His love, so humble and so close, change the way we live.

opts.a: Peace on earth: the angels' song and our reconciliation
intro: On the night of the Nativity the sky over Bethlehem was filled with an army of angels singing glory to God and peace on earth (Luke 2:13–14). Two thousand years later the world still longs for that peace: in the Holy Land where Christ was born, in every land torn by war or communal conflict, and in many of our own homes.
Tonight the Prince of Peace is born. He does not bring peace by force, but by coming close to us, small and defenceless.

sub: Peace is first a gift from God, not an agreement among people.
It comes through a Child: the Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6).
Christ is our peace; he breaks down the walls of hostility (Ephesians 2:14).
points.apply: Ask the Child tonight for the gift of an inner peace that does not depend on circumstances.

sub: Families divided over property, words or old hurts.
Brothers who have not spoken for years.
Couples who live under one roof but far apart.
points.apply: Before the Christmas meal is over, take one step towards someone you are not at peace with.

points.h: Makers of peace in the world
sub: Pray for peace in the Holy Land and wherever there is war.
Refuse hatred and division on social media.
Blessed are the peacemakers (Matthew 5:9).
points.apply: Pray each day of the Christmas season for one country at war.

concl: The angels sang peace on earth among those whom God favours. God's favour rests on all who receive his Son. At this Holy Qurbono, let us exchange the sign of peace with sincerity, and carry it home.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will make peace with one person, and pray daily for one nation at war.
homily: Dear friends, on the night of the Nativity the shepherds heard the angels sing: glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among those whom he favours (Luke 2:14). Glory to God and peace on earth go together. When God is given his glory, peace follows.

Isaiah had called the Child the Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6). Strange prince: born in a stable, laid in a manger, threatened by a king. Yet he brings what no army can bring. St Paul says: he is our peace; in his flesh he has broken down the dividing wall of hostility (Ephesians 2:14).

The world longs for peace. Tonight we pray for the land where Jesus was born, for all places torn by war, and for our own country wherever communities are divided. Christmas is not a holiday from the world's pain; it is God entering it.

But peace begins closer. In many families tonight there is an empty chair, not because of death, but because of a quarrel. Brothers who do not speak, sisters divided over property, a son estranged from his father. The Child in the manger asks: will you let me bring peace into your home?

Jacob, after twenty years of fear, ran to meet his brother Esau, and Esau embraced him (Genesis 33:4). Jesus taught: if your brother has something against you, go first and be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). Christmas is the best time to take that first step: a phone call, a visit, a slice of cake carried across the road.

At this Holy Qurbono, when we offer one another the sign of peace, let it be real. And let us go home as peacemakers, for blessed are the peacemakers; they will be called children of God (Matthew 5:9). A blessed and peaceful Christmas to all. Amen.

opts.a: Good news to the shepherds: Christ comes to the poor and the margins
intro: The first to hear the news of Christmas were not kings or priests, but shepherds: poor, rough, often despised, working through the night. God chose them as the first witnesses of his Son (Luke 2:8–12).
Christmas is good news for all who live at the edges: migrant workers, night-shift nurses, fishermen, farmers, the homeless and the forgotten.

sub: Shepherds were poor and considered unclean.
Yet David, the shepherd boy, became king.
The Good Shepherd is announced first to shepherds.
points.apply: Remember that God's first messengers went to those the world overlooks.

sub: The sign was not power, but a baby in a manger.
God meets us in poverty and simplicity.
The shepherds recognised him because he was like them.
points.apply: Look for Christ this Christmas in a poor person near you.

points.h: They went with haste and told others
sub: The shepherds did not keep the news to themselves.
They returned glorifying and praising God.
The poor became the first evangelisers.
points.apply: Share the joy of Christmas with someone who has no one to celebrate with.

concl: The Child who came first to shepherds comes now to us at this Holy Qurbono. Let us welcome him with simple hearts, and go out like the shepherds to tell others what we have seen.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will share a meal or a gift with a migrant worker, a night worker or a poor family.
homily: Dear friends, on that first Christmas night, while Bethlehem slept, shepherds were keeping watch over their flocks in the fields. To them, not to the powerful in Jerusalem or Rome, an angel appeared and said: do not be afraid; I am bringing you good news of great joy for all the people (Luke 2:10).

Shepherds in those days were poor and often looked down upon. Their work kept them away from the Temple and from respectable company. Yet God chose them. The prophet Ezekiel had promised that God himself would shepherd his people, seek the lost and bind up the injured (Ezekiel 34:11–16). The Good Shepherd announces himself first to shepherds.

The sign they were given was not a palace or a crown, but a child wrapped in bands of cloth and lying in a manger (Luke 2:12). The poor recognised him because he was poor like them. God did not come to the world from above, but from below.

Think of the shepherds of our time: the migrant worker from another state who builds our houses, the nurse on night duty in a hospital abroad, the fisherman at sea on Christmas night, the security guard at the gate, the family in a rented room. Christmas is first their feast.

The shepherds went with haste, found Mary and Joseph and the child, and then made known what had been told them. They returned glorifying and praising God (Luke 2:16–20). The poor became the first evangelists. They had nothing to give but their joy, and it was enough.

At this Holy Qurbono, Christ comes to us as he came to the shepherds: simply, humbly. Let us receive him, and then, like them, go out with haste: to share our Christmas food, to visit someone alone, to bring good news to the margins. A joyful Christmas to all. Amen.

opts.a: A Christmas homily for families and children
intro: This homily is written for a congregation with many children and families. It uses simple words and three images the children can remember: the star, the crib and the gift.
Christmas is a family feast because God chose to be born into a family.

points.h: The star: God shows the way
sub: The star led the wise men to Jesus.
Our Christmas stars remind us: Jesus is the light.
Parents are stars for their children, showing the way to God.
points.apply: Let each family pray together tonight under the Christmas star.

sub: The great God became a little baby.
He chose a poor family and a simple place.
He wants a place in our homes and hearts.
points.apply: Let the children place the Child in the home crib with a prayer.

sub: At Christmas we give gifts because God gave us Jesus.
The best gift is love: time, kindness, forgiveness.
Jesus gives himself again at the Holy Qurbono.
points.apply: Let each person give one gift of love tomorrow that costs no money.

concl: The star shows the way, the crib shows God's humility, and the gift shows his love. May every family leave this Holy Qurbono with the Child in their hearts.
opts.resolve: Our family will pray together before the crib every evening until the end of the Christmas season.
homily: Dear children and dear families, a very happy Christmas to you! Tonight I want to talk about three things you can see around you: the star, the crib and the gift.

First, the star. Look at the stars shining in our homes and in the church. Long ago a star led the wise men to the place where Jesus was (Matthew 2:9–10). Our stars remind us that Jesus is the light of the world. And, dear parents, you are stars for your children: by your prayer and your example, you show them the way to Jesus.

Second, the crib. Look at the crib: Mary, Joseph, the shepherds, the animals, and the little baby. Isn't it amazing? The great God, who made the sun and the stars and the sea, became a tiny baby. He did not choose a palace; he was laid in a manger because there was no room in the inn (Luke 2:7). Children, Jesus wants a place in your home and in your heart. Will you make room for him?

Third, the gift. Why do we give gifts at Christmas? Because God gave us the best gift: his own Son. God so loved the world that he gave his only Son (John 3:16). So our gifts are a little copy of God's love. But the best gifts do not come from a shop: a hug, helping at home, saying sorry, sharing with a poor child.
And there is one more gift. At this Holy Qurbono, Jesus gives himself to us again. The baby of Bethlehem comes to us in Holy Communion. Bethlehem means house of bread, and Jesus is the Bread of Life.

So when you go home tonight, look at the star and say: Jesus, you are my light. Look at the crib and say: Jesus, come into my heart. And give one gift of love tomorrow. A happy and holy Christmas to every family. Amen.

Dear brothers and sisters, two days after Yaldo, the Church takes us into the house at Nazareth. The Son of God did not grow up in a palace. He lived in a small village, in a carpenter's home, with Mary and Joseph, keeping the feasts of his people.

Every year they went up to Jerusalem for the Passover. When Jesus was twelve, he stayed behind in the Temple. Parents here know the fear Mary and Joseph felt: three days of searching! When they found him, Jesus said: “Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” These are his first words in the Gospel. He knew who his true Father was.

And yet the next verse says: “he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them.” The Lord of heaven obeyed a carpenter and a village mother. For about thirty years he lived a hidden life of work, prayer and obedience. Holiness does not begin in great deeds; it begins at home.

Today we also remember the little children killed by Herod. Let us pray for every child in danger: the unborn, children who suffer violence, children of war and hunger. And let us make our homes little Nazareths: with daily family prayer, respect for elders, and joy for children. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was twelve, he went with Mary and Joseph to the big Temple in Jerusalem. On the way home, they couldn't find him! They searched for three days.
They found Jesus in the Temple, listening and asking questions. He said: “This is my Father's house!” Then he went home and obeyed Mary and Joseph.
Jesus obeyed his parents. Can you do that too? Let's say: “Like Jesus, I will love and obey!”

homily: Dear friends, today we celebrate the Immaculate Conception of the Holy Mother of God. The Church believes that from the first moment of her conception, by a singular grace of God and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ, Mary was preserved from every stain of original sin (Pope Pius IX, Ineffabilis Deus, 1854). God prepared a pure dwelling for his Son.

St Paul writes: when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, in order to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children (Galatians 4:4–5). The woman of whom the Son was born is Mary. Her purity serves the Incarnation.

In the Gospel Mary sings her Magnificat: my soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Saviour. Notice: God my Saviour. Mary too was saved by Christ, in a more perfect way: preserved from sin rather than freed from it after falling.

Mary also sings: he has looked with favour on the lowliness of his servant. From now on all generations will call me blessed (Luke 1:48). Our Syriac tradition loves to call her blessed, the Mother of God, the second heaven who carried the Lord of heaven.
Mary's purity is not distance from us. It is the beauty God wants to restore in each of us. Through baptism, confession and the Eucharist, God cleanses us and makes us his children.

During this fast, let us honour Mary by imitating her: humility, purity of heart, faith and praise. Let us make a good confession before Yaldo, so that our hearts too may be a pure dwelling for her Son. Amen.
kids: Children, God kept Mary's heart clean from the very beginning. Ask Mary to help you keep your heart clean too!

opts.a: Mary, the new Eve and the Ark of the Covenant
intro: The Fathers of the Church loved to read the Old Testament with Mary in mind. Two images help us understand this feast: the new Eve and the Ark.

sub: Eve listened to the serpent; Mary listened to the angel.
Eve's disobedience brought death; Mary's obedience opened the way to life.
St Irenaeus: the knot of Eve was untied by Mary.
points.apply: When tempted, say Mary's words: let it be done according to your word.

sub: The Ark held the tablets, the manna and Aaron's rod (Hebrews 9:4).
Mary carried the Word, the Bread of Life, the eternal Priest.
The Ark was made pure; Mary was preserved from all stain.
points.apply: Receive Christ in the Holy Qurbono with a clean heart, like Mary.

sub: God prepared a pure dwelling for His Son.
Mary was redeemed in a more exalted way.
What God did for her, He wants to begin in us.
points.apply: Make a good confession before Christmas.

concl: Mary Immaculate shows us what grace can do and what we are called to be.
The feast in Advent prepares a clean dwelling for Christ in us.
opts.resolve: Before Christmas I will make a good confession to prepare a clean dwelling for Christ.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the early Christians did not have the dogma of the Immaculate Conception in its later words, but they had a deep intuition about Mary, drawn from the Scriptures. Let us look at two images that the Fathers loved: Mary as the new Eve, and Mary as the Ark of the Covenant.

In the garden, Eve listened to the serpent and believed his lie. Through her disobedience, sin and death entered the world. But God promised that the offspring of a woman would crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15). In Nazareth another woman listened, not to a serpent but to an angel, and said: here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word (Luke 1:38). St Irenaeus wrote that the knot of Eve's disobedience was untied by Mary's obedience. Where Eve said no, Mary said yes.

The second image is the Ark of the Covenant. God commanded Moses to make it of acacia wood, covered with pure gold inside and out (Exodus 25:10–11). Inside were the tablets of the law, a jar of manna and Aaron's rod (Hebrews 9:4). When the Ark entered a house, it brought blessing; David danced before it. Mary carried in her womb the Word of God, the true Bread from heaven and the eternal High Priest. When she entered Elizabeth's house, the child leaped for joy (Luke 1:41). If the Ark had to be pure gold, how much more the living Ark of the Son of God.

This is what the Church proclaims today: that from the first moment of her conception Mary was preserved from every stain of original sin, by a singular grace of God and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ. She too was saved by her Son, but in a more exalted way: preserved rather than cleansed.

And what God did perfectly for Mary, He wants to begin in us. In Baptism we were washed; in confession we are cleansed again; in the Holy Qurbono we receive Christ as Mary did. This Advent, let us prepare a clean dwelling for Him. Make a good confession before Christmas, and ask Mary Immaculate to teach you to say yes.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the dogma of the Immaculate Conception
intro: Many people confuse this feast with the virginal conception of Jesus. Let us be clear about what the Church teaches and why.

sub: Defined by Pope Pius IX in 1854 (Ineffabilis Deus).
Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her conception (CCC 491).
By a singular grace, in view of the merits of Christ.
points.apply: Learn the difference between the Immaculate Conception and the Virgin Birth.

sub: The angel's greeting: kecharitomene, highly favoured, filled with grace (Luke 1:28).
Mary was redeemed by her Son (CCC 492).
She remained free of personal sin all her life (CCC 493).
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly, attentive to the words full of grace.

points.h: Lourdes and the faith of the people
sub: 1858: I am the Immaculate Conception.
Eastern tradition: Mary the All-Holy, Panagia (CCC 493).
Our own Churches' devotion to Mary.
points.apply: Honour Mary this Advent with the Rosary.

concl: The dogma honours Christ, whose grace made Mary all-holy.
Mary Immaculate is the model and mother of the Church.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray the Rosary and ask Mary to make my heart pure.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, many Catholics think that today's feast is about the conception of Jesus in Mary's womb. It is not. That we celebrate on 25 March, the Annunciation. Today we celebrate the conception of Mary herself in the womb of her mother, whom tradition names Anne.

On 8 December 1854, Pope Pius IX solemnly defined that the most Blessed Virgin Mary, from the first moment of her conception, by a singular grace and privilege of almighty God, and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ the Saviour of the human race, was preserved free from all stain of original sin (CCC 491). Every word matters. Singular grace: it was God's gift, not Mary's achievement. In view of the merits of Jesus Christ: Mary too was saved by her Son.

Where is this in the Bible? The angel greets Mary as full of grace (Luke 1:28). The Greek word means one who has been, and remains, filled with God's favour. The Church understood that the woman chosen to be the Mother of God was prepared by grace from the beginning. The Catechism says that Mary was redeemed from the moment of her conception, and that by God's grace she remained free of every personal sin her whole life long (CCC 492–493). The Eastern Fathers call her Panagia, the All-Holy.

Four years after the definition, in 1858, Our Lady appeared to a poor girl, Bernadette, at Lourdes. When Bernadette asked her name, she answered: I am the Immaculate Conception. Bernadette did not understand the words, but the parish priest did. Heaven confirmed what the Church had taught.

Why does this matter? Because it shows what God's grace can do. Mary is not a goddess; she is a creature, entirely filled with grace. She shows what the Church is called to become: holy and without blemish (Ephesians 5:27). So let us honour her this Advent with the Rosary, and ask her to help us prepare for her Son at this Holy Qurbono and at Christmas.

Dear friends, the day after Yaldo our Church celebrates the Praise of the Holy Mother of God, honouring Mary who gave birth to the Saviour. The Eastern Churches have always joined the Mother to the feast of her Son.

St Paul writes: when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, so that we might receive adoption as children. And because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba! Father! (Galatians 4:4–6).

Born of a woman. Mary is the bridge by which God entered our humanity. That is why the Church calls her Theotokos, Mother of God: not because she is the source of the divine nature, but because the One born of her is truly God (Council of Ephesus, AD 431).

In the Gospel the shepherds go with haste to Bethlehem and find Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in the manger. They tell what they have heard about the child, and all who hear are amazed. But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:16–19).
Everyone else is talking and wondering. Mary is silent, treasuring, pondering. She keeps the mystery in her heart and lets it grow. This is how she becomes the first disciple.

After the noise of Yaldo, let us learn from Mary to ponder. Let us take a quiet moment each day this week to sit before the crib and treasure what God has done. And let us praise Mary, as our hymns do, as the one who carried the One whom the heavens cannot contain. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary kept everything about Jesus in her heart. Think about baby Jesus quietly for a minute today!

homily: Dear friends, today our Church remembers David, king and prophet. The Letter to the Hebrews lists him among the heroes of faith: Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David and Samuel and the prophets, who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, obtained promises (Hebrews 11:32–33).

Hebrews also remembers those who suffered: they were stoned, sawn in two, killed by the sword; they went about in skins of sheep and goats, destitute, persecuted, tormented, of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:37–38). Faith does not always win in this world; but it always wins with God.

David was a great sinner and a great penitent. He committed adultery and murder, yet when the prophet Nathan confronted him, he repented with all his heart. His psalm of repentance, Psalm 51, is prayed by the Church every day. God promised that the Messiah would come from his line.

In the Gospel Jesus asks the Pharisees: what do you think of the Messiah? Whose son is he? They answer: the son of David. Jesus asks: how is it then that David by the Spirit calls him Lord? (Matthew 22:42–43). The Messiah is David's son, but also David's Lord: truly man and truly God.
The Child of Yaldo is born in the city of David as son of David, yet he is David's Lord and ours. In him the promises to David are fulfilled.

Let us learn from David both his faith and his repentance. When we fall, let us not hide, but return to God with a contrite heart: have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love (Psalm 51:1). Amen.
kids: Children, David was a shepherd boy from Bethlehem who became a king. Jesus, born in Bethlehem too, is our King and Shepherd!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul speaks of a mystery: a hardening has come upon part of Israel, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in. And so all Israel will be saved. For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable (Romans 11:25–26, 29).

God's gifts are irrevocable. God does not take back his promises. Israel remains beloved. And all of us, Jews and Gentiles, have received mercy: God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all (Romans 11:32).

In the Gospel some Pharisees complain that Jesus' disciples do not wash their hands according to the tradition of the elders. Jesus answers: why do you break the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition? He quotes Isaiah: this people honours me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Matthew 15:2–3, 8).

Traditions are precious. Our Church has a beautiful liturgical and spiritual tradition. But tradition must serve love of God and neighbour. When customs become a reason to neglect parents, the poor or justice, they betray God's commandment.

Jesus' example was about children who avoided supporting their parents by declaring their money an offering to God (Matthew 15:5). Religion was used as an excuse not to love. That danger is still with us.

In this Yaldo season, let us check: do I honour God only with my lips, or with my heart? Let us show our faith in caring for our parents, the elderly and the poor. God's gifts to us are irrevocable; let our love be faithful too. Amen.
kids: Children, God loves to forgive. When you say sorry to God, He forgives you completely!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Romans: welcome one another, therefore, just as Christ has welcomed you, for the glory of God (Romans 15:7). Christ welcomed us when we were far from him. We are called to welcome others the same way.
