Paul gathers several Scriptures to show that Christ came for the Gentiles as well as for Israel, and ends with Isaiah: the root of Jesse shall come, the one who rises to rule the Gentiles; in him the Gentiles shall hope. Then he prays: may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit (Romans 15:12–13).

In the Gospel, after Herod's death, an angel tells Joseph in a dream to return to the land of Israel. But fearing Herod's son, Joseph is warned again and goes to Galilee, settling in a town called Nazareth (Matthew 2:19–23).

The Holy Family's life was not settled. Exile in Egypt, return, fear, another change of plan. Joseph had to listen to God again and again. Yet in all this, the family stayed together and the Child grew.
Many of our families live like this: moving for work, uncertain futures, plans that change. The God of hope walks with us. He led Joseph step by step, and he leads us.
As the year ends, let us welcome one another as Christ welcomed us, especially those far from home. And let us ask the God of hope to fill us with joy and peace for the year to come. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus grew up in a small town called Nazareth with Mary and Joseph. Thank God for your family and your home!

homily: Dear friends, on the last day of the year St Paul looks back on his ministry: I have reason to boast in Christ Jesus of my work for God. For I will not venture to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me (Romans 15:17–18).
At the end of a year we look back too. What has Christ accomplished through us? Not what have I achieved, but what has God done through me? Paul's boasting is gratitude.

In the Gospel Jesus tells the parable of a fig tree that bore no fruit for three years. The owner says: cut it down. The gardener pleads: sir, let it alone for one more year, until I dig around it and put manure on it. If it bears fruit next year, well and good; if not, you can cut it down (Luke 13:6–9).
The new year is that one more year: a gift of God's patience. Christ, the gardener, pleads for us and works on our roots through trials, through his word and through the sacraments.

But the parable also carries urgency. God gives time so that we may bear fruit, not so that we may waste it. What fruit is God waiting for from me: reconciliation, prayer, generosity, purity, service?

Tonight let us do three things: thank God for all that Christ has done through us this year, ask pardon for our sins, and make one resolution for the new year. And let us begin the new year in the arms of the Child of Yaldo. Amen.
kids: Children, God gives you a whole new year to grow and do good things. Thank Him tonight and ask Him to bless next year!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the faithful of our Church begin the Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo, the Nativity of our Lord. It is a time of prayer, abstinence and charity, so that our hearts may be a worthy place for the Lord who comes.

St Paul gives us the law of this fast: owe no one anything, except to love one another; for the one who loves another has fulfilled the law. Love does no wrong to a neighbour; therefore love is the fulfilling of the law (Romans 13:8, 10). A fast without love is only a diet.

Paul continues: you know what time it is, how it is now the moment for you to wake from sleep. The night is far gone, the day is near. Let us lay aside the works of darkness and put on the armour of light. Put on the Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 13:11–14).

The Gospel opens with the great hymn of St John: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. In him was life, and the life was the light of all people. The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it (John 1:1–5).

The One we await at Yaldo is not only a child. He is the eternal Word, through whom all things were made. He comes as light into our darkness. Our fast is a way of making room for that light: less food, less noise, less sin, more prayer, more love.

Let us begin this fast with three resolutions: a fast from one food or comfort, a fast from one sin, and one act of love each day. And let us put on the Lord Jesus Christ, like a new garment, as we walk towards Yaldo. Amen.
kids: Children, the fast before Yaldo is a time to get ready for Jesus. Give up something small and do something kind every day!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul asks a chain of questions: how are they to call on one in whom they have not believed? How are they to believe in one of whom they have never heard? How are they to hear without someone to proclaim him? And he answers with Isaiah: how beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news (Romans 10:14–15).
Faith comes through proclamation. Someone told us about Jesus: a mother, a catechist, a priest, a friend. Now it is our turn. The Lord wants beautiful feet that carry good news to others.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks about honesty: do not swear at all. Let your word be yes, yes or no, no; anything more than this comes from the evil one (Matthew 5:34, 37). A disciple does not need oaths, because his ordinary word can be trusted.

These two readings go together. The best proclamation of the Gospel is a truthful life. If our words at work, at home and on social media are not trustworthy, our words about Jesus will not be believed either.
In Kerala we sometimes swear casually: on God, on our mother, on the Bible. Jesus asks for something simpler and harder: be honest always, so that your yes is enough.

During this fast, let us examine our speech. Do I exaggerate, deceive, make promises I do not keep? Let us fast from lies and half-truths, and let our feet carry good news to someone who has not heard it. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus wants us to tell the truth always. When you say yes, mean it; when you promise, keep it!

homily: Dear friends, today we remember St Francis Xavier, the great missionary who preached on the coasts of South India. St Paul describes the heart of a missionary: though I am free with respect to all, I have made myself a slave to all, so that I might win more of them. I have become all things to all people, that I might by all means save some. I do it all for the sake of the gospel (1 Corinthians 9:19, 22–23).

Francis Xavier lived this. He learnt the prayers in the language of the fishermen, sat with the poor, nursed the sick, and walked from village to village. He became one with the people so that they might meet Christ.

In the Gospel the risen Jesus appears to the Eleven and says: go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation. And he promises signs: in my name they will cast out demons, speak in new tongues, lay hands on the sick and they will recover (Mark 16:15–18).
The mission is not finished. Many in our country and in the world have not truly heard the Gospel. Many baptised Christians have forgotten it. The Lord still says: go.

We are not all called to cross oceans, but we are all sent. A Malankara Catholic nurse in Germany, a student in Delhi, a worker in the Gulf, a farmer in Pathanamthitta: each can become all things to all people, out of love for Christ.
Let us pray today for missionaries, and for our own Church's mission in North India and abroad. And let us ask St Francis Xavier to give us his zeal and his joy. Amen.
kids: Children, St Francis Xavier taught children prayers through songs. Teach a prayer or a hymn to a younger child today!

homily: Dear friends, today we remember St John of Damascus, the great Syrian monk and teacher of the faith, who defended the holy icons and wrote beautiful hymns still sung in the Eastern Churches. He taught that because the invisible God became visible in Christ, we may honour images of Christ and his saints.

St Paul writes: faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ (Romans 10:17). Then he quotes Isaiah: I have been found by those who did not seek me (Romans 10:20). God's grace often reaches those we least expect.

In the Gospel Jesus deepens the commandment: you have heard that it was said, you shall not murder. But I say to you that if you are angry with a brother or sister, you will be liable to judgement (Matthew 5:21–22). Anger and insults are the roots of murder.

Then he says something very practical: if you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother or sister has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled, and then come and offer your gift (Matthew 5:23–24).
In our Holy Qurbono we exchange the kiss of peace before the anaphora. This is the moment Jesus speaks of. It is not a formality; it is a commitment to be reconciled.
During this fast, let us look for one broken relationship and take a step towards peace: a phone call, a visit, an apology. Then our offering at Yaldo will be pleasing to God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: make peace first, then come to pray. If you had a fight with someone, say sorry today!

homily: Dear friends, today the Church remembers Mar Saba, the great monk of the Judean desert, and St Clement of Alexandria, an early teacher of the faith. Both trained themselves in godliness.

St Paul tells Timothy: train yourself in godliness, for while physical training is of some value, godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come (1 Timothy 4:7–8). We train our bodies for health; how much more should we train our souls?

The fast is spiritual training. Like an athlete, we practise small disciplines: getting up for prayer, controlling our tongue, saying no to some food, saying yes to charity. These small exercises make the soul strong.

In the Gospel the people are divided about Jesus. Some say he is the prophet, others the Messiah. The temple police, sent to arrest him, return empty-handed and say: never has anyone spoken like this! (John 7:40–46). His words disarmed them.

Nicodemus, who had come to Jesus by night, now speaks up a little for him: our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing (John 7:51). It is a small step of courage, but it is a beginning. Faith often grows by small steps.
This week, let us take one small step of courage for Christ, and one step of training in godliness. The Lord who spoke like no one else still speaks to us in the Gospel. Let us listen. Amen.
kids: Children, athletes train their bodies; Christians train their hearts with prayer and kindness. Train your heart today!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul writes to Timothy from prison: do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord, or of me his prisoner, but join with me in suffering for the gospel, relying on the power of God, who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works but according to his own purpose and grace (2 Timothy 1:8–9).

Paul is chained, yet not ashamed: I know the one in whom I have put my trust, and I am sure that he is able to guard until that day what I have entrusted to him (2 Timothy 1:12). Faith is trusting a Person, not just believing ideas.

In the Gospel, at the Last Supper, Jesus says: the hour is coming, indeed it has come, when you will be scattered, each one to his home, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone because the Father is with me. In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world! (John 16:32–33).

Jesus does not promise his disciples an easy life. He promises his presence and his victory. Many Christians today face hardship for their faith, in parts of India and the world. Many face quieter pressures: mockery at college, unfair treatment at work, loneliness abroad.
Take courage. These are among the last words Jesus spoke before his Passion. The Child we await at Yaldo is the One who has conquered the world.

During this fast, let us not be ashamed of the Gospel. Let us make the sign of the cross before meals in public, speak of our faith when asked, and pray for persecuted Christians. And let us say with Paul: I know the one in whom I have put my trust. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: take courage, I am stronger than everything bad. Do not be afraid to say you love Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews begins majestically: long ago God spoke to our ancestors in many and various ways by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom he also created the worlds (Hebrews 1:1–2).

God spoke through many prophets, each a partial word. In Jesus he speaks his full and final Word. The Son is the reflection of God's glory and the exact imprint of God's very being, and he sustains all things by his powerful word (Hebrews 1:3).

In the Gospel John the Baptist, from prison, sends his disciples to ask: are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another? Jesus answers: go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them (Luke 7:19–22).
God has spoken his final Word in Jesus, and that Word acts: he heals, raises and brings good news to the poor. The signs of the Messiah are works of mercy.
At Yaldo we will see this Word made flesh as a child. The One who sustains the universe will be held in Mary's arms. St Ephrem sang of this wonder in his hymns of the Nativity.

During this fast, let us listen more to the Son: read the Gospel daily. And let us do the works of the Messiah: visit the sick, help the poor, bring good news. Then our lives will answer the question: yes, he has come. Amen.
kids: Children, God speaks to us through Jesus. When we read the Gospel, we hear Jesus speaking to us!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul writes to the Thessalonians: concerning love of the brothers and sisters, you do not need to have anyone write to you, for you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another. But we urge you to do so more and more, to aspire to live quietly, to mind your own affairs, and to work with your hands (1 Thessalonians 4:9–11).
Paul's programme is simple and practical: love more and more, live quietly, do your work well, and do not depend on others. A Christian life is not dramatic; it is faithful in ordinary things.

In the Gospel Jesus tells his disciples three times: do not be afraid. Nothing is covered up that will not be uncovered. Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one will fall to the ground apart from your Father. Even the hairs of your head are all counted. So do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows (Matthew 10:26–31).
God's care is detailed. He knows the sparrow and counts your hair. Nothing in your life escapes his attention. This is the deepest cure for fear.
Then Jesus adds: everyone who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven (Matthew 10:32). Trust in the Father gives us courage to confess the Son.
During this fast, let us bring our fears to the Father who counts our hairs. Let us live quietly, love more and more, and acknowledge Jesus before others without fear. Amen.
kids: Children, God counts every hair on your head! He loves you so much. Never be afraid to say you are a friend of Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul organises a collection for the poor Christians of Jerusalem: on the first day of every week, each of you is to put aside and save whatever extra you earn (1 Corinthians 16:2). Giving is regular, planned and proportional. It is part of Sunday worship.
Our tradition links fasting with almsgiving. What we save by fasting should go to the poor. The twenty-five days' fast is incomplete if it only saves money for ourselves.

In the Gospel the disciples pluck grain on the sabbath because they are hungry, and the Pharisees complain. Jesus reminds them that David ate the holy bread when he was hungry, and then quotes the prophet Hosea: I desire mercy and not sacrifice (Matthew 12:7). He adds: the Son of Man is lord of the sabbath (Matthew 12:8).
Jesus is not against the law. He is against a religion that uses rules to forget people. Rules exist to serve love, not to replace it.

Sometimes we can keep the fast strictly and still be harsh with our families, impatient with the poor, or proud before others. Jesus says: mercy, not only sacrifice. The best fast is the one that makes us more merciful.
This week, let us set aside a portion of what we save by fasting for someone in need. And let us check whether our religion is making us more merciful. Amen.
kids: Children, Sunday is a day for God and for helping others. Save a coin this week for someone in need!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul gives the Thessalonians a list of short commands: respect those who labour among you; be at peace among yourselves; encourage the faint-hearted, help the weak, be patient with all of them. Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you (1 Thessalonians 5:12–18).

Rejoice, pray, give thanks: three practices that can transform a life. Not rejoice when things go well, but always. Not pray when in trouble, but without ceasing. Not give thanks for good things only, but in all circumstances.
Paul adds: do not quench the Spirit. Do not despise the words of prophets, but test everything; hold fast to what is good; abstain from every form of evil (1 Thessalonians 5:19–22).

In the Gospel Jesus speaks strongly: if any of you put a stumbling block before one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for you if a great millstone were hung around your neck and you were thrown into the sea (Mark 9:42). Then he says: if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off (Mark 9:43). These are images of radical seriousness about sin.

Jesus ends: salt is good. Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another (Mark 9:50). Salt gives taste and preserves from decay. A Christian gives flavour to the world and preserves it from corruption.
During this fast, let us remove one stumbling block: a bad habit, a source of temptation, an unhealthy relationship. And let us practise Paul's three words each day: rejoice, pray, give thanks. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul says: be happy, pray always, and say thank you to God. Try all three today!

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews speaks of Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, who met Abraham and blessed him, and to whom Abraham gave a tenth of everything (Hebrews 7:1–2). Melchizedek appears without genealogy, a mysterious figure resembling the Son of God, a priest for ever (Hebrews 7:3).
Melchizedek offered bread and wine (Genesis 14:18). The Church sees in him a figure of Christ, the eternal High Priest, who offers himself under the signs of bread and wine in the Holy Qurbono.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks hard words to the crowds who follow him: whoever comes to me and does not hate father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, and even life itself, cannot be my disciple. Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:26–27).

Hate here is a Semitic way of saying: love less than me. Jesus must come first. Then he gives two examples: a man building a tower first sits down to estimate the cost; a king going to war first considers whether he can win (Luke 14:28–32). Discipleship must be chosen with open eyes.
Today we also remember St John of the Cross, who counted the cost and gave everything for God, finding in the dark night the light of divine love.

During this fast, let us count the cost of following Jesus and choose him again. What do I put before him: family, money, comfort, reputation? Let us give him the first place, so that at Yaldo he may be born in a heart that belongs to him. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus carried His cross because He loves us. When something is hard, offer it to Jesus with love!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Corinthians how he first came to them: I did not come proclaiming the mystery of God to you in lofty words or wisdom. For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified. I came to you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling (1 Corinthians 2:1–3).

Paul was a brilliant scholar, but he did not rely on cleverness. He preached Christ crucified with the power of the Spirit, so that your faith might rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God (1 Corinthians 2:5).

In the Gospel Jesus warns his disciples: they will put you out of the synagogues. Indeed, an hour is coming when those who kill you will think that by doing so they are offering worship to God. I have said these things to you so that when their hour comes you may remember that I told you about them (John 16:2–4).
Religious violence is not new. Jesus foresaw that some would persecute in God's name. Even today, Christians suffer in some places from people who believe they are serving God.

How should we respond? Not with clever arguments or with hatred, but like Paul: with Christ crucified, with humility, with the power of the Spirit. The Child of Yaldo will grow up to be crucified; his weakness is our strength.
During this fast, let us pray for those who persecute Christians and for those who suffer. And let us rely less on our own cleverness and more on the power of God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus on the cross shows us the greatest love. Look at a crucifix today and say: thank you, Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul speaks of a thorn in his flesh. Three times he begged the Lord to take it away, but the Lord said to him: my grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness. So Paul says: I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me; for whenever I am weak, then I am strong (2 Corinthians 12:7–10).

Many of us carry thorns: illness, a difficult family situation, a temptation that returns, a loss that does not heal. We pray, and the thorn remains. God's answer to Paul is also for us: my grace is sufficient.

In the Gospel Jesus is praying alone with his disciples nearby. He asks them: who do the crowds say that I am? They give various answers: John the Baptist, Elijah, one of the prophets. Then he asks: but who do you say that I am? Peter answers: the Messiah of God (Luke 9:18–20).
Notice that this question comes after Jesus has been praying. Knowing who Jesus is comes from prayer, not just from information.

Jesus asks us the same question as Yaldo approaches: who do you say that I am? A baby in a crib? A good teacher? A distant God? Or the Messiah of God, my Lord and Saviour, who gives me grace in my weakness?

During this fast, let us answer Jesus personally, in prayer. And let us bring him our thorns, not only asking for their removal, but asking for the grace to carry them with him. His grace is sufficient. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asks you: who am I for you? Tell Him today: Jesus, you are my friend and my God!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul ends his letter to the Romans with a warning: keep an eye on those who cause dissensions and offences, in opposition to the teaching that you have learned; avoid them. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the simple-minded (Romans 16:17–18).

Then he gives a beautiful promise: the God of peace will shortly crush Satan under your feet (Romans 16:20). This recalls the first promise of salvation in Genesis, that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent's head. At Yaldo that promise begins to be fulfilled.

In the Gospel Jesus says: beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves. You will know them by their fruits. Every good tree bears good fruit, but the bad tree bears bad fruit (Matthew 7:15–17).

Today many voices claim to speak for God: on television, on social media, in new movements. Some bring division, fear and money-making. Jesus gives a simple test: look at the fruits. Do they lead to humility, charity, unity with the Church, and holiness of life?
The test applies to us too. What fruit does my faith bear? Patience at home, honesty at work, generosity to the poor, faithfulness in prayer? A good tree is known not by its leaves but by its fruit.

During the last days of the fast, let us hold fast to the faith we received from the Church, avoid what divides, and ask God to make us good trees. The God of peace will crush evil under our feet. Amen.
kids: Children, a good tree gives good fruit. Be a good tree: do good things today!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul calls himself the very least of all the saints, yet to him this grace was given: to bring to the Gentiles the news of the boundless riches of Christ, and to make everyone see the plan of the mystery hidden for ages in God (Ephesians 3:8–9).

The boundless riches of Christ. At Yaldo we will see these riches in poverty: a baby in a manger. But in him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. The poorer he becomes, the richer we are.

Paul adds that through the Church the wisdom of God in its rich variety might now be made known (Ephesians 3:10). Our Syro-Malankara Church, with its West Syriac heritage, its hymns and its fasts, is part of that rich variety of God's wisdom.

In the Gospel Jesus says: do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me. In my Father's house there are many dwelling places. I go to prepare a place for you. Thomas asks: Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way? Jesus answers: I am the way, and the truth, and the life (John 14:1–6).

Our apostle Thomas asked the honest question, and received the great answer. Jesus is not only a guide who shows the way; he is the way. To follow him is to be already on the road to the Father's house.

As Yaldo approaches, let us bring our troubled hearts to Jesus. Let us thank God for the riches of Christ and for the heritage of our Church. And let us walk with him, the way, the truth and the life. Amen.
kids: Children, the cross is the sign of Jesus' love. Make the sign of the cross slowly and lovingly today!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul writes: Christ is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us. He has reconciled both groups to God in one body through the cross (Ephesians 2:14–16).

Jew and Gentile were deeply divided. Christ did not merely make a truce between them; he created one new humanity in himself. You are no longer strangers and aliens, but citizens with the saints and members of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone (Ephesians 2:19–20).

In the Gospel John the Baptist, in prison, sends to ask Jesus: are you the one who is to come? Jesus answers with signs: the blind see, the lame walk, the poor hear good news. And blessed is anyone who takes no offence at me (Matthew 11:3–6).
John had expected a fiery judge. Jesus came as a healer and peacemaker. Sometimes Jesus does not match our expectations either. Blessed are we if we accept him as he is.

In our country and even in our communities, there are walls: caste, language, region, rite, politics. Christ came to break them down. The Child of Yaldo was visited by Jewish shepherds and Gentile Magi: the first sign of one new humanity.
In these last days before Yaldo, let us break down one wall: reach out to someone from a different background, community or Church. And let us accept Jesus as he comes, not as we imagine him. Amen.
kids: Children, God wants to live in your heart. Make your heart a nice home for Jesus by being kind and loving!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul begins his letter to the Romans with thanksgiving: I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the world (Romans 1:8). He longs to see them, so that we may be mutually encouraged by each other's faith (Romans 1:12).

Faith is not a private possession; it grows through sharing. When we pray together, visit each other and speak about God, we encourage one another. Paul, the great apostle, also needed the encouragement of ordinary believers.

Paul says: I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish (Romans 1:14). He felt he owed the Gospel to everyone. We too are debtors: we received the faith freely, and we owe it to others.

The Gospel today is the prologue of John: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. In him was life, and the life was the light of all people (John 1:1–4). Four days before Yaldo, the Church lifts our eyes from the manger to eternity.

The Child we will adore is the eternal Word. Through him all things were made, including you and me. When we hold the image of the Child in our homes, we are looking at the Creator who became a creature out of love.
In these last days, let us encourage someone in their faith: a phone call, a visit, a word of hope. And let us repay our debt by sharing the light we have received. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus made everything: the sun, the stars and you! Say thank you to Jesus for everything He made.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul is troubled about the Galatians: formerly, when you did not know God, you were enslaved to beings that by nature are not gods. Now that you have come to know God, or rather to be known by God, how can you turn back again to the weak and beggarly elemental spirits? (Galatians 4:8–9).
Notice how Paul corrects himself: you have come to know God, or rather to be known by God. Faith begins not with our knowing God but with God knowing us. He knew us before we knew him.

Paul is worried because the Galatians were going back to old religious observances as a way of earning salvation: you are observing special days, and months, and seasons, and years (Galatians 4:10). Our fasts and feasts are good, but they do not save us. Only Christ saves.

In the Gospel John introduces John the Baptist: there was a man sent from God, whose name was John. He came as a witness to testify to the light, so that all might believe through him. He himself was not the light (John 1:6–8). The true light, which enlightens everyone, was coming into the world (John 1:9).

John the Baptist knew he was not the light. Our fast, our customs, our Church buildings and even our preachers are not the light. They point to Christ, the true light. We must not stop at the signpost.

As the fast comes to an end, let us ask: has my fast been a way of earning God's favour, or of opening my heart to his grace? Let us thank God that he knows us, and let us turn our eyes from the signposts to the light. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist pointed to Jesus. You can point to Jesus by being kind, so that others see His love in you!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Colossians how much he struggles for them and for those at Laodicea, so that their hearts may be encouraged and united in love, so that they may have all the riches of assured understanding and have the knowledge of God's mystery, that is, Christ himself, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (Colossians 2:1–3).
All the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Christ. Two days before Yaldo, they are hidden in a child about to be born. God hides his greatest treasures in humble places.

Paul warns: I am saying this so that no one may deceive you with plausible arguments (Colossians 2:4). Faith needs both love and understanding. A believer who knows Christ well is not easily deceived.

In the Gospel John writes: he was in the world, and the world came into being through him; yet the world did not know him. He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him. But to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God (John 1:10–12).

These are among the saddest and most hopeful words in the Bible. The Creator came to his own creation, and it did not recognise him. But to all who received him, he gave the power to become children of God.

In two days we will celebrate his coming. Will we receive him? Let us make room: a good confession, reconciliation, quiet prayer, charity to someone in need. And let us become what he came to make us: children of God. Amen.
kids: Children, there was no room for Jesus at the inn. Make room for Jesus in your heart by saying a prayer every night!

homily: Dear friends, on the Eve of Yaldo St Paul speaks frankly about the human condition: the wrath of God is revealed against all ungodliness and wickedness of those who by their wickedness suppress the truth. Ever since the creation of the world his eternal power and divine nature have been understood and seen through the things he has made (Romans 1:18, 20).

Paul says that humanity knew God through creation but did not honour him: they became futile in their thinking, and their senseless minds were darkened. They exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images (Romans 1:21–23). This is why the world needed a Saviour.

The Gospel gives God's answer: the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth. From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, who has made him known (John 1:14–18).
Humanity exchanged God's glory for images. Tonight, God gives us the true image of himself: a Child in a manger. Humanity's darkened mind is enlightened by the Word made flesh.

Tonight our parishes will celebrate the service of Yaldo with joy. The fast ends. Stars shine on our homes. But let us not lose the heart of the feast: God has come close. The invisible God has become visible.
Before the celebrations begin, let us find a quiet moment to kneel before the crib and say: Lord, you came for me. Thank you. Let us receive tonight grace upon grace. A blessed Yaldo to all. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight Jesus, the Son of God, is born as a little baby! Welcome Him with joy and tell Him you love Him.

intro: Theme: “What then will this child become?”

Elizabeth's son is born, and a family argument about a name becomes a moment of faith. The birth of John teaches us that every child is a gift, that obedience opens our lips to praise, and that every life has a mission in God's plan.

points.h: Every child is a gift from God
sub: The neighbours rejoice because the Lord has shown great mercy to Elizabeth.
Hannah, after long prayer, gave her son back to the Lord.
Children are not property or burdens; they are God's heritage entrusted to us.
q: Sons are indeed a heritage from the LORD, the fruit of the womb a reward.
All who heard them pondered them and said, “What then will this child become?” For, indeed, the hand of the Lord was with him.
points.apply: Bless your children each night with the sign of the Cross.

points.h: Obedience opens our lips to praise
sub: Zechariah writes, “His name is John,” meaning “God is gracious”, against family custom.
At once his tongue is freed, and he blesses God.
When we obey God's word, even against pressure, our silence turns into praise.
q: For this child I prayed; and the LORD has granted me the petition that I made to him. Therefore I have lent him to the LORD.
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And all of them were amazed. Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue freed, and he began to speak, praising God.
points.apply: Where are you silent because of disobedience? Obey, and find your voice of praise.

points.h: Every life has a mission: to prepare the way
sub: John will be “the prophet of the Most High”, going before the Lord.
God makes his people a crown of beauty in his hand.
Each of us is sent to prepare a way for Christ in our home, work and nation.
q: You shall be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.
And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways.
points.apply: Ask in prayer: “Lord, for whom am I to prepare your way this Christmas?”

concl: Zechariah's song ends with light: the dawn from on high will break upon those in darkness and guide our feet into the way of peace.
May our families welcome every child as a gift, obey God's word, and prepare the way for the Lord.
2026-12-06.resolve: Pray Zechariah's Benedictus (Luke 1:68–79) each morning this week.

intro: Theme: “Joseph: the just man who listened and obeyed.”
Joseph never speaks a word in the Gospels, yet his silence is full of faith. Faced with a crisis he did not understand, he chose mercy, listened to God in the night, and acted at once.

sub: Joseph discovers that Mary is with child and does not understand.
Being righteous, he will not expose her to disgrace: his justice is clothed in mercy.
Micah sums up God's will: do justice, love kindness, walk humbly.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
Her husband Joseph, being a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, planned to dismiss her quietly.
points.apply: In a family conflict this week, choose the way that protects the other's dignity.

sub: While Joseph is still deciding, the angel speaks in a dream.
Like the boy Samuel, Joseph has a listening heart.
God still speaks in silence, in Scripture, in conscience and through the Church; we must make room to listen.
q: Now the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
An angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.”
points.apply: Before sleeping, spend five minutes in silence with the Lord, without your phone.

sub: Joseph wakes and does exactly as the angel commanded.
He takes Mary into his home and gives the child the name Jesus, “God saves”.
Fathers of families are called to the same quiet courage: to protect, provide and lead their homes to God.
q: Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth! For I am God, and there is no other.
When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took her as his wife.
points.apply: Fathers: pray with your family this week and bless your children.

concl: St Joseph teaches us that holiness is often silent: justice with mercy, listening in the night, obedience in the morning.
As Christmas draws near, let us ask him to guard our families as he guarded the Holy Family.
2026-12-13.resolve: Entrust your family to St Joseph each day this week with an Our Father.

intro: Theme: “The shoot from the stump of Jesse.”

The Sunday before Christmas gives us a long list of names: the genealogy of Jesus. It looks dry, but it tells a great truth: God keeps his promises through real families, with their saints and their sinners, until the Saviour is born.

points.h: God writes salvation through a human family tree
sub: Matthew begins with Abraham and David: God's promise runs through generations.
The list includes sinners and foreigners: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, the wife of Uriah. God's grace works through broken stories.
From a cut-down stump, Isaiah says, a new shoot will grow: no family history is beyond God's hope.
q: A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots.
An account of the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
points.apply: Thank God for your family's faith, and pray for its wounds this week.

points.h: A righteous King from David's house
sub: Jeremiah promised a righteous Branch who would do justice.
Joseph, of the house of David, goes to Bethlehem with Mary because of an emperor's decree.
God uses even the plans of the powerful to fulfil his own.
q: The days are surely coming, says the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and he shall reign as king and deal wisely, and shall execute justice and righteousness in the land.
Joseph also went from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, because he was descended from the house and family of David.
points.apply: Trust God in the events you cannot control; he is still guiding history.

sub: Isaiah's vision: the wolf and the lamb together, no harm on God's holy mountain.
The angels will sing peace to those whom God favours.
Christmas peace begins in our homes: reconciliation before celebration.
q: They will not hurt or destroy on all my holy mountain; for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among those whom he favors!
points.apply: Before Christmas, make peace with one person and make a good confession.

concl: The long genealogy ends in a manger. God has been faithful through every generation, and he is faithful to us.
Let us prepare our hearts and homes, so that the shoot of Jesse may grow in us.
2026-12-20.resolve: Set up the crib at home this week and pray before it as a family.

intro: Theme: “The light has come: receive him.”

Tonight the whole Church sings: a child is born for us. The eternal Word, through whom all things were made, lies in a manger. Three movements of the feast: light in darkness, God made small, and our response of welcome and worship.

sub: Isaiah saw a people walking in darkness and promised a great light.
John proclaims Christ as the true light that enlightens everyone.
Whatever darkness we carry tonight (sin, sickness, grief, fear), the light has come for us.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who lived in a land of deep darkness—on them light has shined.
The true light, which enlightens everyone, was coming into the world.
points.apply: Bring one dark area of your life to the crib and ask the Child to enlighten it.

sub: Not Jerusalem but little Bethlehem; not a palace but a manger.
There was no room in the inn: God comes humbly and can be refused.
His smallness is an invitation: we can approach him without fear.
q: But you, O Bethlehem of Ephrathah, who are one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel, whose origin is from of old, from ancient days.
He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him. But to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God.
points.apply: Make room for Christ in someone who is poor or alone this Christmas.

sub: Isaiah names the Child: Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Prince of Peace.
The Magi kneel, worship and offer gold, frankincense and myrrh.
Our gift is ourselves: our faith (gold), our prayer (incense), our sacrifices (myrrh).
q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
On entering the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother; and they knelt down and paid him homage. Then, opening their treasure chests, they offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
points.apply: Kneel before the Child in the Holy Qurbono and receive him worthily.

concl: The Word became flesh and dwelt among us. The God whom no one has ever seen has shown us his face in a child.
Let us receive him, adore him and carry his light into the new year.
2026-12-25.resolve: Each day of the Christmas octave, kneel briefly before the crib and say: “Jesus, be born in my heart.”

intro: Theme: “The Holy Family: a home where God grows.”
After Christmas the Church looks at the home where Jesus grew up. The Son of God chose to live thirty years in an ordinary family at Nazareth. Our families can become holy in the same ordinary ways.

points.h: A family that goes to God's house together
sub: Every year Mary and Joseph went up to Jerusalem for the Passover.
At twelve, Jesus stays in the Temple: “I must be in my Father's house.”
Parents first teach children to love God's house by going there gladly themselves.
q: I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the LORD!”
He said to them, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?”
points.apply: Come to the Holy Qurbono as a whole family, on time, every Sunday.

sub: Jesus returns to Nazareth and is obedient to Mary and Joseph.
Proverbs teaches children to listen to a father's instruction and a mother's teaching.
Mary treasures everything in her heart: family life needs reflection and prayer, not only work.
q: Hear, my child, your father's instruction, and do not reject your mother's teaching.

Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart. And Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.
points.apply: Children: obey your parents with a cheerful heart this week. Parents: spend unhurried time with your children.

points.h: A family protected by God through trials
sub: The Holy Family knew danger, exile and fear.
Joseph rises at God's word and brings them safely home.
God promises to dwell among his people “in faithfulness and in righteousness”.
q: I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They shall be my people and I will be their God, in faithfulness and in righteousness.
Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who were seeking the child's life are dead.
points.apply: Pray together for families in crisis: separated, sick, in debt or abroad.

concl: Nazareth teaches us silence, work and love. Holiness grows at the family table, in prayer together and in daily obedience.
May Jesus, Mary and Joseph make our homes little Nazareths.
2026-12-27.resolve: Begin or renew evening family prayer, and consecrate your family to the Holy Family.

intro: Theme: “Put on the Lord Jesus Christ.”
The first day of the Christmas fast.

sub: Leviticus: love your neighbour as yourself.
Paul: love is the fulfilling of the law.
q: you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore, love is the fulfilling of the law.
points.apply: Join your fast to one act of love each day.

sub: Isaiah: your light has come.
Paul: put on the armour of light.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
the night is far gone, the day is near. Let us then lay aside the works of darkness and put on the armor of light;
points.apply: Give up one habit of the night during the fast.

sub: God said: let there be light.
The Word was God, and the light shines.
q: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
points.apply: Read John 1:1–18 slowly each Sunday of the fast.

concl: The fast prepares a home for the Word.
Let love be its heart.
2026-12-01.resolve: Keep the fast with prayer, fasting and alms every day.

intro: Theme: “How beautiful are the feet.”
Sent messengers with truthful tongues.

sub: Jeremiah protested he was only a boy.
Paul: how will they hear without a preacher?
q: But the LORD said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am only a boy’; for you shall go to all to whom I send you, and you shall speak whatever I command you.
But how are they to call on one in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in one of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone to proclaim him?
points.apply: Share one sentence of faith with someone this week.

sub: The law demanded that vows be kept.
Jesus asks for a plain yes or no.
q: When a man makes a vow to the LORD, or swears an oath to bind himself by a pledge, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth.
Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.
points.apply: Keep one promise exactly today.

sub: Lying lips are an abomination to God.
Do not swear at all.
q: Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, but those who act faithfully are his delight.
But I say to you, Do not swear at all, either by heaven, for it is the throne of God,
points.apply: Speak only the truth today.

concl: Messengers of the Word must be truthful.
Let the fast purify our tongues.
2026-12-02.resolve: Fast from lies and harsh words for the whole fast.

intro: Theme: “Go into all the world.”
St Francis Xavier and the missionary heart.

points.h: Called and held by the hand
sub: God calls his servant in righteousness.
Paul becomes all things to all.
q: I am the LORD, I have called you in righteousness, I have taken you by the hand and kept you;
To the weak I became weak, so that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all people, that I might by all means save some.
points.apply: Listen patiently to someone very different from you.

sub: Declare his glory among the nations.
Proclaim the good news to the whole creation.
q: Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples.
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.
points.apply: Pray for a missionary from your eparchy.

sub: Isaiah: the blind see, the lame leap.
Signs accompany those who believe.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy.
And these signs will accompany those who believe: by using my name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new tongues;
points.apply: Do one work of mercy for a sick person.

concl: The Gospel came to our shores through missionaries.
Now we are sent.
2026-12-03.resolve: Support the missions with prayer or alms during this fast.

intro: Theme: “First be reconciled.”
Peace before the altar.

sub: The psalm warns against wrath.
Jesus names anger as liable to judgment.
q: Refrain from anger, and forsake wrath.
But I say to you that if you are angry with a brother or sister, you will be liable to judgment;
points.apply: Notice and offer to God one moment of anger today.

sub: Isaiah: cease to do evil, learn to do good.
Jesus: be reconciled, then offer.
q: cease to do evil, learn to do good;
leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.
points.apply: Take one step toward reconciliation.

points.h: Found by those who did not seek
sub: God let himself be found.
Faith comes from hearing.
q: I was ready to be sought out by those who did not ask, to be found by those who did not seek me.
So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.
points.apply: Listen to the Scripture readings at the next Qurbono with full attention.

concl: God first reconciled us to himself.
Let us carry that peace to others.
2026-12-04.resolve: Make peace with one person before Christmas.

intro: Theme: “Never has anyone spoken like this.”
Training in godliness, listening to the Word.

sub: Joshua was to meditate on the law day and night.
Godliness holds promise for this life and the next.
q: This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth; you shall meditate on it day and night,
for, while physical training is of some value, godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.
points.apply: Add five minutes of silent prayer to each day of the fast.

sub: The psalmist thirsts for the living God.
Paul toils because his hope is in him.
q: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.
For to this end we toil and struggle, because we have our hope set on the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe.
points.apply: Offer your fasting as a prayer of hope.

sub: God promised a prophet who would speak his words.
The police say no one has spoken like Jesus.
q: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their own people; I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet, who shall speak to them everything that I command.
The police answered, “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
points.apply: Read one Gospel chapter slowly today.

concl: The fast trains us; the Word disarms us.
Let us listen to Jesus.
2026-12-05.resolve: Read the whole Gospel of Luke during the fast, a few verses each day.

intro: Theme: “Take courage; I have conquered the world.”
Faith guarded and peace given.

points.h: I shall not be put to shame
sub: The Servant sets his face like flint.
Paul knows the one he has trusted.
q: The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;
But I am not ashamed, for I know the one in whom I have put my trust,
points.apply: Make the sign of the cross in public today.

sub: Hold on to instruction; it is your life.
Guard the good deposit with the Spirit's help.
q: Keep hold of instruction; do not let go; guard her, for she is your life.
Guard the good treasure entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit living in us.
points.apply: Teach one prayer or truth of faith to a child.

sub: God promised Joshua his presence.
Jesus has overcome the world.
q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.
I have said this to you, so that in me you may have peace. In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!
points.apply: Hand one fear to Jesus in prayer.

concl: We know whom we have believed.
His victory is our peace.
2026-12-07.resolve: Pray each night of the fast: Jesus, I trust in you.

intro: Theme: “The Mighty One has done great things for me.”
Mary, preserved from sin for her Son.

sub: God promised enmity between the serpent and the woman.
In the fullness of time the Son is born of a woman.
q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, in order to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children.
points.apply: Thank God for the gift of Mary as our mother.

sub: Hannah sang her joy in the Lord.
Mary sings the Magnificat.
q: My heart exults in the LORD; my strength is exalted in my God.
And Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior,
points.apply: Pray the Magnificat slowly today.

sub: The Song: there is no flaw in you.
Mary praises the holiness of God's name.
q: You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you.
for the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.
points.apply: Make a good confession before Yaldo.

concl: God prepared a pure mother for his Son.
Let him prepare our hearts too.
2026-12-08.resolve: Pray one Hail Mary each day of the fast for purity of heart.

intro: Theme: “Are you the one who is to come?”
God's final Word answers with works.

sub: The psalm sees the Lord seated at God's right hand.
Hebrews: God has spoken by a Son.
q: The LORD says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”

Long ago God spoke to our ancestors in many and various ways by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom he also created the worlds.
points.apply: Read Hebrews 1 slowly today.

sub: Isaiah: the Spirit anoints the Servant.
Jesus points to the signs of the kingdom.
q: The spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed,
And he answered them, “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised,
points.apply: Do one work of mercy for a poor or sick person.

sub: The stone the builders rejected became the cornerstone.
Blessed is the one who takes no offence.
q: The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone.
And blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me.
points.apply: Tell Jesus honestly one doubt you carry.

concl: God's last Word is his Son.
His works answer our doubts.
2026-12-09.resolve: Note each evening one sign of God's goodness.

intro: Theme: “Do not be afraid.”
Martyrs' courage and everyday love.

sub: God promises to strengthen and uphold.
Fear only the one who can destroy soul and body.
q: do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
points.apply: Name one fear and give it to God.

sub: God knit us together in the womb.
We are worth more than many sparrows.
q: For it was you who formed my inward parts; you knit me together in my mother's womb.
So do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.
points.apply: Thank God for one way he has cared for you.

sub: God writes his law on the heart.
The Thessalonians are taught by God to love.
q: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts;
Now concerning love of the brothers and sisters, you do not need to have anyone write to you, for you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another;
points.apply: Do one hidden act of love at home.

concl: God counts every hair.
Let us not be afraid to acknowledge him.
2026-12-10.resolve: Pray each day for persecuted Christians.

intro: Theme: “I desire mercy and not sacrifice.”
The Lord's Day, the poor, and mercy.

sub: The law commands generosity to the poor.
Paul: put aside something every Sunday.
q: Since there will never cease to be some in need on the earth, I therefore command you, “Open your hand to the poor and needy neighbor in your land.”
On the first day of every week, each of you is to put aside and save whatever extra you earn, so that collections need not be taken when I come.
points.apply: Give the money saved by fasting to the poor.

sub: The priest gave David the holy bread.
Jesus: mercy, not sacrifice.
q: So the priest gave him the holy bread; for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence,
But if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the guiltless.
points.apply: Share a meal with someone who is alone.

sub: Remember the sabbath day.
The Son of Man is its Lord.
q: Remember the sabbath day, and keep it holy.
For the Son of Man is lord of the sabbath.
points.apply: Plan next Sunday around worship, family and rest.

concl: The holy day is fulfilled in mercy.
Let our fast feed the hungry.
2026-12-11.resolve: Keep every Sunday of the fast with the Qurbono and an act of mercy.

intro: Theme: “Have salt in yourselves.”
A rule of life for the fast.

sub: His steadfast love endures forever.
Rejoice, pray and give thanks in all circumstances.
q: O give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever.
Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
points.apply: Repeat a short prayer throughout the day.

sub: God promised to pour out his Spirit on all.
Test everything; hold fast to the good.
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh;
Do not quench the Spirit. Do not despise the words of prophets, but test everything; hold fast to what is good;
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit each morning.

sub: Every offering was seasoned with salt.
Have salt in yourselves and be at peace.
q: You shall not omit from your grain offerings the salt of the covenant with your God;
Salt is good; but if salt has lost its saltiness, how can you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.
points.apply: Make peace with one person this week.

concl: Joy, prayer and thanks are God's will.
Let us be salt and peace.
2026-12-12.resolve: Give thanks to God for three things each night of the fast.

intro: Theme: “Carry the cross and follow me.”
The eternal Priest and the cost of discipleship.

sub: Melchizedek brought bread and wine.
He resembles the Son of God, a priest forever.
q: And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.
Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
points.apply: Receive Holy Communion this week with special attention.

sub: The psalmist lifts the cup in thanks.
The disciple carries the cross.
q: What shall I return to the LORD for all his bounty to me? I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the LORD,
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
points.apply: Bear one difficulty today without complaining.

sub: By wisdom a house is built.
Count the cost before building.
q: By wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established;
For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not first sit down and estimate the cost, to see whether he has enough to complete it?
points.apply: Complete one resolution you made for this fast.

concl: Christ the eternal Priest goes before us with his cross.
Let us follow to the end.
2026-12-14.resolve: Make the Way of the Cross on Friday.

intro: Theme: “Jesus Christ, and him crucified.”
The power of God in weakness.

sub: Isaiah: he was wounded for our transgressions.
Paul knows only Christ crucified.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
points.apply: Pray five minutes before a crucifix today.

sub: Jeremiah: let the wise not boast in wisdom.
Paul: faith rests on God's power.
q: Do not let the wise boast in their wisdom, do not let the mighty boast in their might, do not let the wealthy boast in their wealth; but let those who boast boast in this, that they understand and know me,
My speech and my proclamation were not with plausible words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit and of power, so that your faith might rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit before speaking about faith.

sub: Those who love God's law have great peace.
Jesus speaks to keep us from stumbling.
q: Great peace have those who love your law; nothing can make them stumble.
I have said these things to you to keep you from stumbling.
points.apply: Pray for persecuted Christians.

concl: The crib and the cross are God's power.
Let our faith rest there.
2026-12-15.resolve: Pray before a crucifix each day until Yaldo.

intro: Theme: “My grace is sufficient for you.”
Confessing Christ; strong in weakness.

points.h: Who do you say that I am?
sub: God alone is Lord.
Peter confesses the Messiah of God.
q: I am the LORD, and there is no other; besides me there is no god.
He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Messiah of God.”
points.apply: Write in one sentence who Jesus is for you.

sub: God gives strength to the powerless.
His grace is sufficient.
q: He gives power to the faint, and strengthens the powerless.
but he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.”
points.apply: Bring one persistent weakness to God.

sub: Flesh and heart may fail; God remains.
When I am weak, then I am strong.
q: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
Therefore I am content with weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and calamities for the sake of Christ; for whenever I am weak, then I am strong.
points.apply: Thank God for one weakness that taught you to trust him.

concl: Jesus asks for our answer.
His grace is enough for our weakness.
2026-12-16.resolve: Say each morning: Lord, your grace is enough for me.

intro: Theme: “You will know them by their fruits.”
Discernment and the victory of the God of peace.

sub: Jeremiah warned of prophets speaking their own visions.
Jesus: wolves in sheep's clothing.
q: Thus says the LORD of hosts: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you; they are deluding you. They speak visions of their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
points.apply: Check religious content for faithfulness before sharing it.

sub: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.
Be wise in good, guileless in evil.
q: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight.
For while your obedience is known to all, so that I rejoice over you, I want you to be wise in what is good and guileless in what is evil.
points.apply: Read one page of the Catechism this week.

sub: The psalm: you will trample the serpent.
Paul: the God of peace will crush Satan.
q: You will tread on the lion and the adder, the young lion and the serpent you will trample under foot.
The God of peace will shortly crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal rejection of Satan in prayer tonight.

concl: Test the fruits.
The God of peace is stronger than evil.
2026-12-17.resolve: Do one act of kindness each day until Yaldo.

intro: Theme: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”
The cross and the Father's house.

points.h: A dwelling in the Father's house
sub: The psalmist hopes to dwell in God's house forever.
Jesus prepares many dwelling places.
q: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I shall dwell in the house of the LORD my whole life long.
In my Father's house there are many dwelling places. If it were not so, would I have told you that I go to prepare a place for you?
points.apply: Pray for the dead of your family.

sub: Isaiah: a voice says, this is the way.
Jesus: I am the way.
q: And when you turn to the right or when you turn to the left, your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it.”
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
points.apply: Ask Jesus to show you the way in one decision.

sub: The least of the saints preaches the riches of Christ.
The cross reached India early.
q: My dwelling place shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Although I am the very least of all the saints, this grace was given to me to bring to the Gentiles the news of the boundless riches of Christ,
points.apply: Venerate the cross in your home tonight.

concl: The cross is the way to the Father's house.
Let us walk it with St Thomas.
2026-12-18.resolve: Make the sign of the cross with attention each morning and night.

intro: Theme: “A dwelling place for God.”
The last Saturday before Yaldo.

sub: Ezekiel: my dwelling shall be with them.
Paul: you are built into God's dwelling.
q: My dwelling place shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
in whom you also are built together spiritually into a dwelling place for God.
points.apply: Prepare your home's prayer corner for Yaldo.

sub: Isaiah: peace to the far and the near.
Christ proclaimed peace to both.
q: Peace, peace, to the far and the near, says the LORD; and I will heal them.
So he came and proclaimed peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near;
points.apply: Invite someone who is alone to share Christmas with you.

points.h: The deaf hear, the blind see
sub: Isaiah foretold the healing of the senses.
Jesus points to his works.
q: On that day the deaf shall hear the words of a scroll, and out of their gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind shall see.

Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John what you hear and see: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news brought to them.
points.apply: Tell someone one thing Jesus has done for you.

concl: God comes to dwell with us.
Let us prepare the house.
2026-12-19.resolve: Make a good confession before Yaldo if you have not yet done so.

intro: Theme: “The life was the light of all people.”
Shared faith and the Creator made child.

points.h: To the end of the world
sub: Creation's voice goes out through all the earth.
The Romans' faith is proclaimed everywhere.
q: yet their voice goes out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the world.
points.apply: Send a Christmas message that speaks of Jesus.

sub: Qoheleth: one lifts up the other.
Paul: mutual encouragement in faith.
q: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil. For if they fall, one will lift up the other;
or rather so that we may be mutually encouraged by each other's faith, both yours and mine.
points.apply: Visit or call someone whose faith is weak.

points.h: By the word of the Lord
sub: The heavens were made by God's word.
All things came into being through the Word.
q: By the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of his mouth.
All things came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being. What has come into being in him was life, and the life was the light of all people.
points.apply: Thank God for creation under tonight's sky.

concl: The Creator comes as a child.
Let us share the light of faith.
2026-12-21.resolve: Read John 1:1–18 every day until Yaldo.

intro: Theme: “The true light was coming into the world.”
Witnesses to the light, known by God.

sub: Malachi: I send my messenger to prepare the way.
John came as a witness to the light.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me,
There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. He came as a witness to testify to the light, so that all might believe through him.
points.apply: Put a light in your window as a sign of Christ.

sub: The psalmist: the Lord is my light; whom shall I fear?
John: the true light enlightens everyone.
q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?
The true light, which enlightens everyone, was coming into the world.
points.apply: Bring one fear into the light of Christ.

sub: God knew Jeremiah before he formed him.
The Galatians are known by God.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you,
Now, however, that you have come to know God, or rather to be known by God, how can you turn back again to the weak and beggarly elemental spirits?
points.apply: Pray Psalm 139 tonight.

concl: We are known by God before we know him.
Let us point others to the light.
2026-12-22.resolve: Light a candle at family prayer each night until Yaldo.

intro: Theme: “He gave power to become children of God.”
Rejected and received.

sub: Isaiah's Servant was rejected.
His own did not accept him.
q: He was despised and rejected by others; a man of suffering and acquainted with infirmity;
He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him.
points.apply: Welcome someone who is usually left out.

sub: God promised David's heir: I will be a father to him.
In Christ we become children of God.
q: I will be a father to him, and he shall be a son to me.
But to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God,
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises tonight.

sub: The Lord gives wisdom.
All its treasures are hidden in Christ.
q: For the LORD gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding;
Christ himself, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
points.apply: Spend quiet time before the crib tomorrow.

concl: There was no room at the inn; let there be room in us.
Receive him and become God's child.
2026-12-23.resolve: Prepare a crib at home and pray before it.

intro: Theme: “The Word became flesh.”
The vigil of Yaldo.

sub: God's glory filled the tabernacle.
The Word pitched his tent among us.
q: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Come to the Yaldo Qurbono with a prepared heart.

sub: The Lord is merciful and gracious.
From his fullness we receive grace upon grace.
q: The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness,
From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. The law indeed was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Thank God for three graces received this year.

sub: Creation proclaims God's handiwork.
God's power is seen in what he made.
q: The heavens are telling the glory of God; and the firmament proclaims his handiwork.
Ever since the creation of the world his eternal power and divine nature, invisible though they are, have been understood and seen through the things he has made.
points.apply: Keep Christ, not things, at the centre of Christmas.

concl: God has pitched his tent among us.
Let us kneel before him tonight.
2026-12-24.resolve: Spend time before the crib each day of the Christmas season.

intro: Theme: “Mary treasured all these words.”
Praise of the Mother of God.

sub: Isaiah: the young woman shall bear a son, Immanuel.
Through her Son we cry “Abba! Father!”
q: Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
And because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, “Abba! Father!”
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly with your family.

sub: Micah: from Bethlehem shall come a ruler.
The shepherds hurry to Bethlehem.
q: But you, O Bethlehem of Ephrathah, who are one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel,
So they went with haste and found Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in the manger.
points.apply: Visit the crib in your parish church.

sub: The psalmist treasures God's word in his heart.
Mary ponders all these things.
q: I treasure your word in my heart, so that I may not sin against you.
But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
points.apply: Sit before the crib in silence for ten minutes.

concl: Mary gave us the Saviour.
With her, let us keep and ponder.
2026-12-26.resolve: Pray one decade of the Rosary each day of the Christmas season.

intro: Theme: “Whose son is he?”
David and the Messiah.

sub: God promised David an everlasting kingdom.
Jesus is acknowledged as David's son.
q: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me; your throne shall be established forever.
“What do you think of the Messiah? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “The son of David.”
points.apply: Thank God for keeping his promises to you.

sub: David calls the Messiah “my lord”.
Jesus is both son and Lord.
q: The LORD says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”
If David thus calls him Lord, how can he be his son?
points.apply: Adore Christ as Lord before the crib.

points.h: In the name of the Lord
sub: David faced Goliath in the Lord's name.
By faith the heroes conquered kingdoms.
q: But David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with sword and spear and javelin; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
points.apply: Bring one great difficulty to God in the Lord's name.

concl: David's hope is fulfilled in Bethlehem.
Let our faith rest in the Son of David.
2026-12-28.resolve: Pray one psalm each day of the Christmas season.

intro: Theme: “Merciful to all.”
Irrevocable calling, mercy for all, hearts not only lips.

sub: God loves his people with an everlasting love.
His gifts and calling are irrevocable.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
for the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
points.apply: Pray for the Jewish people and for Christian unity.

sub: The Lord is slow to anger and full of love.
God shows mercy to all.
q: The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.
For God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all.
points.apply: Forgive one person this Christmas.

sub: Isaiah: lips near, hearts far.
Jesus repeats Isaiah's warning.
q: The Lord said: Because these people draw near with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me,
This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me; in vain do they worship me, teaching human precepts as doctrines.
points.apply: Slow down and mean each word at your next prayer.

concl: God's mercy reaches everyone.
Let our hearts be near him.
2026-12-29.resolve: Do one concrete act of care for your parents or elders this week.

intro: Theme: “The God of hope.”
Welcome, obedience and hope at the year's end.

sub: The law: love the alien as yourself.
Paul: welcome one another as Christ welcomed you.
q: The alien who resides with you shall be to you as the citizen among you; you shall love the alien as yourself,
Welcome one another, therefore, just as Christ has welcomed you, for the glory of God.
points.apply: Welcome a newcomer in your parish or neighbourhood.

points.h: Out of Egypt I called my son
sub: Hosea: God called his son out of Egypt.
Jesus settles in Nazareth.
q: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
There he made his home in a town called Nazareth, so that what had been spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled, “He will be called a Nazorean.”
points.apply: Do one duty promptly today, like Joseph.

sub: Isaiah: the nations shall seek the root of Jesse.
Paul: the God of hope fills us with joy.
q: On that day the root of Jesse shall stand as a signal to the peoples; the nations shall inquire of him,
May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Name three reasons for hope as the year ends.

concl: God keeps his promises in hidden ways.

intro: Theme: “One more year.”
God's patience and our fruit.

sub: Joel: rend your hearts, for God is gracious.
The gardener pleads for one more year.
q: rend your hearts and not your clothing. Return to the LORD, your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love,
He replied, ‘Sir, let it alone for one more year, until I dig around it and put manure on it.

sub: God did everything for his vineyard.
The tree must bear fruit.
q: What more was there to do for my vineyard that I have not done in it?
If it bears fruit next year, well and good; but if not, you can cut it down.
points.apply: Choose one fruit to bear in the new year.

sub: Teach us to count our days.
Paul offers his work as priestly service.
q: So teach us to count our days that we may gain a wise heart.
to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
